checkOnOpen.description: Look for new breakpoints when the project opens; nothing is written without you.
checkOnOpen.help: Look for breakpoints the config does not have when the project opens and offer them in a notice; nothing is written without you. Off analyses only on command.
checkOnOpen.label: Check when opening

edgeViews.description: Also propose a view 1 px below each boundary.
edgeViews.help: Also propose a view 1 px below each breakpoint boundary, to catch layouts that break just before a media query applies. Off proposes the boundaries only.
edgeViews.label: Views at the edges

mergeTolerancePx.description: Boundaries closer than this many px count as one.
mergeTolerancePx.help: Boundaries closer together than this many pixels count as one proposal, so 767 and 768 do not become two views. Raise it for noisy stylesheets.
mergeTolerancePx.label: Merge tolerance

mode.description: One view per breakpoint, five groups, or a view at every edge.
mode.help: What the breakpoint analyser proposes from a page's media queries: all gives one view per breakpoint, groups five device classes, edges a view at every boundary. Start with all.
mode.label: Proposal mode

static.description: Also read breakpoints from Tailwind, Bootstrap and SCSS sources.
static.help: Also read breakpoints from the project's Tailwind, Bootstrap, SCSS and Less sources, not only from the loaded CSS. Off reads the running pages only.
static.label: Scan project files

staticGlobs.description: The project files read for Tailwind, Bootstrap, SCSS and Less breakpoints, as globs relative to the project (node_modules and dot folders are never read).
staticGlobs.help: The project files read for Tailwind, Bootstrap, SCSS and Less breakpoints, as globs relative to the project; node_modules and dot folders are never read. Example: src/styles/**/*.scss.
staticGlobs.label: Project files to scan

urls.description: Pages to analyse besides the start URL.
urls.help: Further pages the analyser reads besides the start URL, so breakpoints of product or article templates are found too. Example: /products/1, /blog/first-post.
urls.label: Further URLs

actionTimeoutMs.description: How long one action of a flow - a click, a fill, a wait for an element - may wait, in milliseconds, before it fails and names its element. Never longer than the flow timeout.
actionTimeoutMs.help: How long one action of a flow (a click, a fill, a wait for an element) may wait, in milliseconds, before the flow fails with the element it waited for, instead of running out of the whole flow timeout. It is never longer than the flow timeout; page loads may take the flow timeout. Example: 20000 for a slow development server.
actionTimeoutMs.label: Action timeout

dir.description: Where the flows of the project live: .rbrowser/flows or a folder inside it, which workspace trust covers.
dir.help: Where the project's flows live, as a folder below .rbrowser/, which workspace trust covers. Example: .rbrowser/flows. Flows outside it are not run.
dir.label: Flows folder

parallel.description: How many views run a flow at the same time; 0 runs all views at once.
parallel.help: How many views run a flow at the same time; 0 runs it in every view at once. Lower it to 1 or 2 when a flow hits a rate-limited server.
parallel.label: Views at once

screenshotOnFailure.description: Save a screenshot of each view whose flow failed or timed out, beside result.json.
screenshotOnFailure.help: Saves a screenshot of each view whose flow failed or timed out, beside result.json, so you see what the page showed. Off saves only the result.
screenshotOnFailure.label: Screenshot on failure

syncDuringRun.description: Keep syncing input between the views while a flow runs. Off, the views of the run do not sync, so no action happens twice.
syncDuringRun.help: Keeps the input sync on while a flow runs. Off, the views of the run do not sync, so a flow's clicks are not replayed twice. Leave it off unless a flow relies on the sync.
syncDuringRun.label: Sync during a flow

timeoutMs.description: How long a flow may run in one view, in milliseconds. A flow's // @timeout comment overrides it.
timeoutMs.help: How long a flow may run in one view, in milliseconds, before it is stopped as failed. A flow's own // @timeout comment overrides it. Example: 60000 for a minute.
timeoutMs.label: Flow timeout

dir.description: Where recordings are saved, relative to the project root. It must lie inside .rbrowser/ and outside the folders workspace trust protects (flows, snippets, plugins, mocks, scripts). An existing recording is never overwritten.
dir.help: Where recordings are saved, relative to the project root: inside .rbrowser/ and outside the folders workspace trust protects (flows, snippets, plugins, mocks, scripts). An existing recording is never overwritten.
dir.label: Recordings folder

playbackPace.description: How Play runs a recording and how its export waits: fast, or with the pauses as recorded.
playbackPace.help: Fast runs the steps back to back, each waiting only for its element. As recorded keeps the pause before each step as it was recorded, at most 10 seconds each - in Play and in the exported flow and test. The choice beside Play in the Recorder panel starts here.
playbackPace.label: Playback pace

recordAutofill.description: Record what Form autofill fills while a recording runs: each field as a fill, check or select step with the value set, in the views it filled. Password and secret fields are recorded as placeholders.
recordAutofill.help: Form autofill fills by script, which the recorder does not capture as input. On, each field it fills during a recording becomes a step with the value it set, so a flow made from the recording fills the form the same way. Password fields and the secret fields are recorded as placeholders, as with typing.
recordAutofill.label: Record form autofill

recordHover.description: Keep a hover as a step when it opened what the next click hits, such as a menu. Other pointer moves are never recorded.
recordHover.help: Keep a hover as a step when it opened what the next click hits, such as a menu, so the replay can open it too. Other pointer moves are never recorded.
recordHover.label: Record menu hovers

recordScroll.description: Record scrolling as steps, consecutive scrolls of the page or an element as one.
recordScroll.help: Record scrolling as steps of a flow, consecutive scrolls of the page or of one element merged into one. Off leaves scrolling out, so recordings stay short.
recordScroll.label: Record scrolling

secretFields.description: Further fields whose values are never recorded, besides password fields: a CSS path as the recorder shows it (#otp), [data-testid="..."] or the field's accessible name. Their values are recorded as a placeholder named after the field. An entry also names a URL query or fragment parameter whose value is recorded masked.
secretFields.help: Fields whose values are never written into a recording, besides password fields: a CSS path (#otp), [data-testid="..."] or the field's accessible name. Also a URL parameter whose value is masked. Example: #otp, token.
secretFields.label: Secret fields

dir.description: Where exported flows and Playwright tests are written, relative to the project root. It must lie inside .rbrowser/ and outside the folders workspace trust protects (flows, snippets, plugins, mocks, scripts). Each export gets a new folder; nothing is overwritten.
dir.help: Where exported flows and Playwright tests are written, relative to the project root: inside .rbrowser/ and outside the folders workspace trust protects. Each export gets a new folder.
dir.label: Exports folder

includeConfig.description: Write a playwright.config.ts beside an exported test, with one project per breakpoint (viewport, pixel ratio, touch, user agent, locale, colour scheme).
includeConfig.help: Write a playwright.config.ts beside an exported test, with one Playwright project per breakpoint (viewport, pixel ratio, touch, user agent, locale, colour scheme), so the test runs outside rBrowser as recorded.
includeConfig.label: Write playwright.config.ts

locatorPreference.description: Which way of finding an element the exported code prefers when the element has it: test id, role and name, text or CSS path. Auto takes the recorder's best one.
locatorPreference.help: Which locator the exported Playwright code prefers when the element offers it: test id, role and name, text or CSS path. Auto takes the recorder's best guess per element.
locatorPreference.label: Preferred locator

bookmarks.description: Pages the team checks often. A path is put after the URL of the current environment; a URL stays the same. config.local.json adds your own by id. Each may have a group and a shortcut.

followEnvironment.description: A new bookmark of a page that lies under one of the project's environments stores only the path (/shop/cart?x=1#top), so it opens on whichever environment is in effect. A page of a foreign host stays a whole URL. Off, every new bookmark is a whole URL.
followEnvironment.help: Lets one bookmark serve local, staging and production: Bookmark this page stores the path without the host when the page belongs to an environment of the project, and the bookmark opens on the environment you switched to. Off stores the whole URL as before. Existing bookmarks are never changed silently; Ctrl+Shift+Space, P, P turns them into paths.
followEnvironment.label: New bookmarks follow the environment

bookmarks.help: Pages the team opens often, listed in the toolbar and the palette. A path such as /checkout is appended to the current environment, a full URL stays as it is. Each may carry a group and its own shortcut.
bookmarks.label: Bookmarks

newViewModifier.description: Shift or Ctrl: held with a click in the size quick pick, or with a project's own breakpoint shortcut that does not contain it already, it opens a new view instead of changing the active one. Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9 contain both already.
newViewModifier.help: Shift or Ctrl: held with a click in the size quick pick or with a project's own breakpoint shortcut, it opens a new view instead of changing the active one. Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9 contain both already.
newViewModifier.label: New-view modifier

overlayMs.description: How long the overlay naming the breakpoint stays, in milliseconds.
overlayMs.help: How long the overlay naming the breakpoint stays on a view after a breakpoint shortcut, in milliseconds. 0 shows none.
overlayMs.label: Breakpoint overlay duration

breakpoints.description: The breakpoints in display order: size, engine and emulation of each view. A breakpoint that names a device preset may leave out its width and height; the preset's viewport fills them. Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9 follow this order.
breakpoints.help: The views of the grid: one per entry, with its width, height, engine, session and emulation. Example: mobile 390 x 844 on Chromium, desktop 1440 wide on Firefox. Ctrl+Shift+1 to 9 pick them in this order.
breakpoints.label: Breakpoints

enabled.description: Messages a page sends with window.__rbrowser.bus reach the same page in the other views, never the sender and only pages of the same origin.
enabled.help: Lets a page send messages with window.__rbrowser.bus that reach the same page in the other views of the same origin, for example to sync app state the input sync cannot see. Off drops them.
enabled.label: Message bus

maxPayloadBytes.description: The largest payload of one message, in bytes of its JSON text. bus.send throws for a larger one.
maxPayloadBytes.help: The largest message the bus accepts, in bytes of its JSON text; a larger one makes bus.send throw. Example: 65536 for 64 KiB. Keep it small so a chatty page cannot flood the other views.
maxPayloadBytes.label: Largest payload

maxPerSecond.description: How many messages a view may send per second; bus.send drops the rest and returns false.
maxPerSecond.help: How many bus messages a view may send per second; the rest are dropped and bus.send returns false. Raise it for pages that stream state, lower it to protect slow machines.
maxPerSecond.label: Messages per second

defaultDelay.description: Seconds to wait before a screenshot from a shortcut, the toolbar or the palette, for example to open a hover menu first. The delay command cycles it for the session.
defaultDelay.help: Seconds to wait before a screenshot taken by shortcut, toolbar or palette, for example to open a hover menu first: 0, 5 or 10. The delay command cycles it for the session.
defaultDelay.label: Delay

dir.description: The folder screenshots are saved to. Empty uses .rbrowser/out/screenshots in the project. A project may only name a folder inside the project; your user settings may also name an absolute folder.
dir.help: The folder screenshots are saved to. Empty uses .rbrowser/out/screenshots inside the project. A project may only name a folder inside itself; your user settings may name any folder, such as D:\shots.
dir.label: Screenshot folder

elementPadding.description: Space around an element screenshot, in CSS pixels on every side.
elementPadding.help: Space around an element screenshot on every side, in CSS pixels, so a button keeps its shadow and context. 0 crops to the element's box.
elementPadding.label: Element padding

freezeAnimations.description: Freeze CSS animations, transitions, the text caret and videos (paused on their first frame) with prefers-reduced-motion during each capture, so two captures of the same page match. Everything runs again afterwards.
freezeAnimations.help: Freeze CSS animations, transitions, the caret and videos (on their first frame) during each capture with prefers-reduced-motion, so two captures of the same page match. Off captures moving content as it is.
freezeAnimations.label: Freeze animations

hideBanners.description: Hide cookie banners, consent dialogs and chat widgets before each capture: screenshots, visual regression, sitemap capture and the environment comparison. They are shown again afterwards.
hideBanners.help: Hide cookie banners, consent dialogs and chat widgets before every capture (screenshots, visual regression, sitemap, environment comparison) and show them again afterwards. Off captures the page as it is.
hideBanners.label: Hide cookie banners

hideSelectors.description: The project's own elements to hide before each capture, as CSS selectors, in addition to the built-in list.
hideSelectors.help: The project's own elements to hide before each capture, as CSS selectors, in addition to the built-in list. Example: #newsletter-popup, .live-chat.
hideSelectors.label: More elements to hide

overviewLabels.description: Show the label, size, engine and environment above each view in the overview image.
overviewLabels.help: Show label, size, engine and environment above each view in the overview image, so a reviewer knows what they look at. Off gives bare images.
overviewLabels.label: Labels in the overview

pathPattern.description: The file name below the folder, without .png. Write each placeholder in curly braces: date (date and time of the run), day, time, env, breakpoint, view, mode, width, height, dpr. A slash starts a folder.
pathPattern.help: The file name below the folder, without .png, from placeholders in braces: date, day, time, env, breakpoint, view, mode, width, height, dpr. A slash starts a folder. Example: day, a slash, then env and breakpoint, each in braces, gives one folder per day.
pathPattern.label: File name pattern

settleMs.description: How long to wait after hiding and freezing before the capture, in milliseconds (0 to 5000).
settleMs.help: How long to wait after hiding banners and freezing animations before the capture, in milliseconds (0 to 5000), so layout shifts settle. Raise it for pages that reflow slowly.
settleMs.label: Settle time

useBuiltinList.description: Hide the elements of rBrowser's built-in list of common consent managers (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, Didomi, Borlabs, Klaro, CookieYes, Complianz and others) and chat widgets.
useBuiltinList.help: Hide the elements of rBrowser's built-in list of consent managers (OneTrust, Cookiebot, Usercentrics, Didomi, Borlabs, Klaro and others) and chat widgets. Off relies on your own selectors only.
useBuiltinList.label: Use the built-in list

autoplay.description: The Videos panel starts a recording as soon as you choose it.
autoplay.help: On: choosing a recording in the Videos panel plays all its views at once. Off: it waits at the start for Play.
autoplay.label: Play recordings when chosen

fps.description: The frame rate of the files. A frame the page did not repaint is repeated, so the video keeps the recorded length.
fps.help: The frame rate of recorded videos. 30 suits most reviews; 60 shows animations smoothly at twice the file size. A frame the page did not repaint is repeated.
fps.label: Frames per second

keepDays.description: After each recording, rBrowser recordings older than this many days are deleted. 0 keeps all. A project's value only ever keeps more than yours.
keepDays.help: How long rBrowser keeps recordings in .rbrowser/out/video. After each new recording those older than this many days are deleted; 0 keeps them however old. With Keep recordings set too, either limit deletes. If the project config sets it too, the value that keeps longer wins (0 the longest), so a checked-in project never deletes more than you allow.
keepDays.label: Keep recordings for (days)

keepRecordings.description: After each recording only this many of the newest rBrowser recordings are kept; older ones are deleted. 0 keeps all. A project's value only ever keeps more than yours.
keepRecordings.help: How many recordings rBrowser keeps in .rbrowser/out/video. After each new recording the oldest beyond this number are deleted, files and folder; the one just made and one still running are always kept, and files rBrowser did not record are never touched. 0 keeps every recording. If the project config sets it too, the value that keeps more wins (0 the most), so a checked-in project never deletes more than you allow.
keepRecordings.label: Keep recordings

maxDurationSec.description: A recording stops by itself after this many seconds, and its files are written completely.
maxDurationSec.help: A recording stops by itself after this many seconds and its files are written completely, so a forgotten recording cannot fill the disk. Example: 300 for five minutes.
maxDurationSec.label: Longest recording

quality.description: Image quality from 1 to 100, of the captured frames and of the encoder. Higher gives larger files.
quality.help: The image quality of the captured frames and the encoder, 1 to 100. 80 is a good balance; raise it for pixel-exact reviews, lower it for small files.
quality.label: Video quality

enabled.description: Let external tools such as Playwright connect over the Chrome DevTools Protocol, protected by a token.
enabled.help: Lets external tools such as Playwright connect to the views over the Chrome DevTools Protocol through a token-protected proxy. Off refuses every connection. Copy the endpoint with Ctrl+Shift+Space, comma, E.
enabled.label: CDP proxy

port.description: A fixed port for the CDP proxy; a random free port when empty.
port.help: A fixed port for the CDP proxy on 127.0.0.1, so a script can keep one endpoint. Example: 9333. Empty picks a free port at every start.
port.label: CDP port

axe.description: The axe-core rule tags to run (for example wcag22aa).
axe.label: Accessibility check

ignore.description: Findings to leave out: each entry matches a rule id, a page URL and an element selector (globs, * for any text); every field it names has to match.
ignore.help: Findings to leave out of every report: each entry names a rule id, a page URL and an element selector as globs (* for any text), and every field it names has to match. Example: rule a11y-axe.*, url */admin/*.
ignore.label: Ignored findings

keepRuns.description: How many check runs stay under .rbrowser/out/checks/; older ones are removed.
keepRuns.help: How many check runs stay under .rbrowser/out/checks/; older ones are deleted when a new run starts. Raise it to keep a longer history for comparisons.
keepRuns.label: Runs kept

lighthouse.help: Which Lighthouse categories a run measures: performance, accessibility, best-practices and seo. Tick the ones you need; none ticked runs all four. Throttling is set under the Lighthouse plugin.
lighthouse.label: Lighthouse

parallel.description: How many check plugins run at once, counted per view.
parallel.help: How many check plugins run at the same time per view. Lower it to 1 or 2 on a slow machine; higher finishes a run sooner.
parallel.label: Checks at once

rules.description: Per rule id (plugin.rule): off, or the severity its findings get.
rules.help: Switch single rules off or change the severity of their findings, by rule id in the form plugin.rule. Example: seo.title-length to warning, fonts.small-text to off.
rules.label: Rule overrides

items.description: Your own device presets: viewport, pixel ratio, user agent, platform, touch. A breakpoint that names a preset as its device takes every value it leaves out from the preset, width and height included; what the breakpoint sets itself wins. Picking a preset for the active view sizes it to the preset's viewport.
items.help: Your own device presets: id, label, viewport, pixel ratio, user agent, platform, touch, orientation. A breakpoint that names a preset takes every value it leaves out from it. Example: id kiosk, 1080 x 1920, dpr 1, touch.
items.label: Device presets

replaceDefaults.description: Use only your own device presets instead of adding them to the built-in list.
replaceDefaults.help: Use only your own device presets, instead of adding them to the built-in list of phones, tablets and desktops. On, the quick pick shows your presets alone.
replaceDefaults.label: Replace built-in devices

dockHeight.description: The height of DevTools docked below the grid, in pixels. Drag the bar between the grid and DevTools to change it; the grid keeps at least a quarter of the window.
dockHeight.help: The height of DevTools docked below the grid, in pixels; dragging the bar between grid and DevTools changes it. The grid keeps at least a quarter of the window.
dockHeight.label: Dock height

dockWidth.description: The width of DevTools docked beside the grid, in pixels. Drag the bar between the grid and DevTools to change it; the grid keeps at least a quarter of the window.
dockWidth.help: The width of DevTools docked beside the grid, in pixels; dragging the bar changes it. The grid keeps at least a quarter of the window.
dockWidth.label: Dock width

followActiveView.description: Docked DevTools inspect whichever view is active.
followActiveView.help: Docked DevTools switch to whichever view becomes active, so one panel inspects the view you work in. Off keeps them on the view you opened them for.
followActiveView.label: Follow the active view

mode.description: Docked below the grid, docked beside it, or in a window of their own.
mode.help: Where DevTools open: docked below the grid, docked beside it, or in a window of their own. Docked DevTools can follow the active view.
mode.label: DevTools position

openOnInspect.description: Open DevTools for the view when Inspect element is chosen while they are closed or with another view, then select the element. Off, Inspect only selects in DevTools already open for that view.
openOnInspect.help: Whether Inspect element in a page's context menu, or its shortcut, may open DevTools. On (the default), DevTools open for the clicked view where the DevTools mode says - or move there from another view - and the element under the click is selected. Off, Inspect never opens or moves DevTools: the element is selected only when DevTools are already open for that view; otherwise the menu entry is disabled and the shortcut says in the status bar that nothing was inspected. The MCP tool devtools_inspect_at always opens DevTools, whatever this says.
openOnInspect.label: Inspect opens DevTools

screencast.description: Show the inspected page once more inside docked DevTools, in Chrome's screencast beside the panels. Off, the panels take the whole dock and the element inspector picks in the view itself. Changing it opens the dock again.
screencast.help: Whether docked DevTools show Chrome's screencast of the page beside the panels. Off (the default) gives the panels the whole dock and lets the element inspector pick in the view itself; on shows the page a second time. A change reopens the dock.
screencast.label: Screencast in DevTools

colorScheme.help: The prefers-color-scheme every breakpoint without its own reports: light or dark. Set it to dark to review the dark theme in every view at once; empty follows the system.
colorScheme.label: Colour scheme

cpuThrottling.description: Slow the CPU of every view down by this factor (4 is four times slower); 1 is none.
cpuThrottling.help: Slows every view's CPU by this factor to see how the page performs on a weak phone; 4 is four times slower, as Lighthouse's mobile preset. 1 is full speed.
cpuThrottling.label: CPU throttling

defaultCpuThrottling.description: The factor the CPU shortcut sets on a view that has no throttling.
defaultCpuThrottling.help: The slowdown factor the CPU shortcut sets on a view without throttling; 4 is four times slower, as Lighthouse's mobile preset.
defaultCpuThrottling.label: CPU throttling of the shortcut

defaultGeolocation.description: The location preset (built in or your own) the location shortcut sets on a view that has none.
defaultGeolocation.help: The location preset the location shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Space, E, G) sets on a view that has none: berlin, new-york, tokyo, sydney or the id of one of your own presets.
defaultGeolocation.label: Location of the shortcut

defaultTimezone.description: The IANA time zone the time zone shortcut sets on a view that has none.
defaultTimezone.help: The IANA time zone the time zone shortcut sets on a view that has none. Example: Europe/Berlin, Asia/Tokyo.
defaultTimezone.label: Time zone of the shortcut

dpr.description: The DPR every breakpoint without its own gets.
dpr.help: The device pixel ratio of breakpoints that set none, so images and media queries see a retina or a plain screen. Example: 2 for a MacBook, 3 for an iPhone. Empty leaves the engine's own.
dpr.label: Device pixel ratio

geolocation.description: The location every view reports to navigator.geolocation, without asking; only the page's own origin gets the permission. Empty is the real one.
geolocation.help: The position every view reports to navigator.geolocation without asking, for store finders and maps. Example: latitude 52.52, longitude 13.405 for Berlin. Empty is the real position.
geolocation.label: Location

geolocationPresets.description: Your own locations (id, label, latitude, longitude, accuracy), offered beside Berlin, New York, Tokyo and Sydney. One with a built-in id replaces it.
geolocationPresets.help: Your own locations for the location shortcut and the palette: id, label, latitude, longitude, accuracy. One with a built-in id (berlin) replaces it. Example: id hq, 48.137, 11.575.
geolocationPresets.label: Location presets

headers.description: Extra request headers for every view. Headers from config.json and config.local.json apply only in a trusted workspace; an untrusted workspace sends only headers set live.
headers.help: Extra request headers every view sends, for example a basic-auth or a feature-flag header for staging. Applies from config files only in a trusted workspace; headers set live apply always.
headers.label: Request headers

locale.description: BCP 47 locale for Intl, navigator.language and Accept-Language.
locale.help: The language every breakpoint without its own reports (Intl, navigator.language, Accept-Language), so dates, numbers and translations show for that market. Example: de-DE, en-GB.
locale.label: Locale

media.description: Reduced data and transparency, forced colours, contrast, colour gamut and the print media type.
media.help: Further media features of breakpoints without their own: prefers-reduced-data and -transparency, forced-colors, prefers-contrast, color-gamut and the media type. Example: mediaType print to review print styles.
media.label: Further media features

mobile.description: Emulate a mobile device: meta viewport and overlay scrollbars.
mobile.help: Whether breakpoints without their own setting load as a mobile device: the meta viewport applies and scrollbars overlay the page. Usually on together with touch for phone breakpoints.
mobile.label: Mobile device

network.description: A preset (offline, slow 3G, fast 3G, 4G) or your own latency and throughput.
network.help: The network conditions of every view: a preset such as slow 3G or fast 3G, or your own latency and throughput. Use it to see loading states and lazy images as a mobile user does. Empty is the real network.
network.label: Network throttling

offline.description: Take every view offline: navigator.onLine is false and requests fail. Switching it off restores the network without a new view.
offline.help: Takes every view offline: navigator.onLine is false and every request fails. Use it to review offline pages and service-worker caches; switching it off brings the network back at once.
offline.label: Offline

orientation.help: Portrait or landscape for breakpoints without their own; the screen orientation API and the orientation media query follow it. Example: landscape to review a tablet turned sideways.
orientation.label: Orientation

paper.description: The paper of a print view: A4 is 794 px wide, Letter 816 px (at 96 dpi). It sizes a breakpoint that leaves its width or height out.
paper.help: The paper of a print view, which sizes a breakpoint that leaves out its width or height: A4 is 794 px wide, Letter 816 px at 96 dpi. Pair it with mediaType print to review print layouts.
paper.label: Paper

platform.description: navigator.platform and the client hints platform.
platform.help: What navigator.platform and the client hints report for breakpoints without their own, so scripts that branch on the OS see the one you test. Example: Win32, MacIntel, iPhone.
platform.label: Platform

reducedMotion.help: Whether breakpoints without their own report prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, so you see the page as a user who switched animations off. Off reports no preference.
reducedMotion.label: Reduced motion

safeAreas.description: The insets of a notch or home indicator, in CSS px.
safeAreas.help: The notch and home-indicator insets breakpoints without their own report through env(safe-area-inset-*), in CSS px. Example: top 47, bottom 34 for an iPhone. Empty reports none.
safeAreas.label: Safe-area insets

textScale.description: The accessibility font scaling; 1 is none.
textScale.help: The accessibility font scaling of breakpoints without their own, as a factor; 1.3 shows the page as a user with larger system text sees it. 1 is no scaling.
textScale.label: Text scale

timezone.description: The IANA time zone every view reports (Intl, Date), such as America/New_York. Empty keeps the system's.
timezone.help: The time zone every view reports through Intl and Date, so booking and calendar pages show the local time of a market. Example: America/New_York. Empty keeps the system's.
timezone.label: Time zone

touch.description: Emulate touch: touch events, maxTouchPoints and pointer: coarse.
touch.help: Whether breakpoints without their own setting behave as a touch device: touch events, maxTouchPoints and pointer: coarse. Switch it on to see hover-free navigation and larger tap targets.
touch.label: Touch input

userAgent.description: The user agent string; empty keeps the engine's own.
userAgent.help: The user agent string every breakpoint without its own sends and reports, so server-side device detection sees a phone or a desktop. Example: an iPhone Safari string. Empty keeps the engine's.
userAgent.label: User agent

allowWebStore.description: Install extensions from the Chrome Web Store by id or store URL (the field below, Extensions: install from the Chrome Web Store, a trusted project's recommendations). Each one is downloaded from Google's update server, its CRX3 signatures are checked against the developer's key and the Web Store's, and it is unpacked under rBrowser's local folder and loaded at the next start. An MCP client's install always asks you in the window first. Off hides the field and refuses the commands; what is installed stays loaded.
allowWebStore.help: Whether an extension may be installed from the Chrome Web Store by id or URL. Each download is verified against the developer's key and the Web Store's signature before it is unpacked; an MCP client's install always asks in the window. Off hides the field and refuses the commands; installed extensions stay.
allowWebStore.label: Install from the Chrome Web Store

checkUpdatesAtStart.description: At every start, ask the Chrome Web Store whether an installed extension has a newer version; an update is installed only after you confirm it in the window. Off checks only on Extensions: check the Chrome Web Store for updates.
checkUpdatesAtStart.help: Whether rBrowser asks the Chrome Web Store at every start for newer versions of the installed extensions (one download per extension). An update is installed only after you confirm it. Off (the default) checks only on the command Extensions: check the Chrome Web Store for updates.
checkUpdatesAtStart.label: Check for extension updates at start

enabled.description: Load the unpacked extensions below into every Chromium view. Off loads none and keeps the list. The change takes effect at the next start.
enabled.help: Loads the unpacked extensions listed below into every Chromium view. Off loads none and keeps the list for later. Applies at the next start.
enabled.label: Chrome extensions

offerProjectRecommendations.description: A trusted project's recommended extensions are named in a notice; they are added only by the command Extensions: add the project's recommendations, never by themselves.
offerProjectRecommendations.help: A trusted project's recommended extensions are named in a notice when it opens; they are added only by the command Extensions: add the project's recommendations. Off shows no notice.
offerProjectRecommendations.label: Offer a project's recommended extensions

unpacked.description: Folders of Manifest V3 extensions (the folder with manifest.json), loaded where they are, not copied. Only add extensions you trust: an extension runs its code in every page of every Chromium view. Changes take effect at the next start.
unpacked.help: Folders of Manifest V3 extensions (the folder with manifest.json), loaded where they are. Example: C:\dev\vue-devtools\build. Only add extensions you trust: they run in every page of every Chromium view. Applies at the next start.
unpacked.label: Unpacked extensions

sandbox.description: Run the Chromium processes in the sandbox. Switch it off only when the sandbox fails on this machine. The change takes effect at the next start; while the sandbox is off, the log notes it at every start.
sandbox.help: Runs Chromium's renderer processes in the Windows sandbox, which protects the machine from a malicious page. Switch it off only when the sandbox fails here; the log then notes it at every start. Applies at the next start.
sandbox.label: Chromium sandbox

copy.description: When the cookies of a Chromium session are copied into its Firefox and WebKit views: by hand (Copy cookies, Ctrl+Shift+Space, E, J), into each Firefox or WebKit view as it starts, or after each page load of a Chromium view.
copy.help: When a Chromium session's cookies are copied into its Firefox and WebKit views: manual only on command (Ctrl+Shift+Space, E, J), on start as each external view starts, or after each page load of a Chromium view.
copy.label: Copy cookies to Firefox and WebKit

domainFilter.description: Only the cookies of the sites the views show and of the current environment, or every cookie of the session.
domainFilter.help: Which cookies are copied: environment takes only those of the sites the views show and of the current environment, all takes every cookie of the session.
domainFilter.label: Cookies to copy

exclude.description: Cookie names (* matches any text, as in _ga*) or domains, which cover their subdomains, that are never copied.
exclude.help: Cookie names (* for any text, as in _ga*) or domains, which cover their subdomains, that are never copied into Firefox and WebKit. Example: _ga*, analytics.example.com.
exclude.label: Never copy

reload.description: A Firefox or WebKit view that got cookies loads its page again, so the page sees them.
reload.help: A Firefox or WebKit view that received cookies reloads its page, so the page sees the login. Off leaves the page until its next navigation.
reload.label: Reload after copying

embed.description: Experimental: Firefox and WebKit views sit in their grid cells like Chromium views: the window has no frame, menu, tabs or address bar, follows its cell and shows the page at the breakpoint's width scaled to the cell. Off (default): every such view is a window of its own beside the main window.
embed.help: Experimental. Shows each Firefox and WebKit view in its grid cell: its window is owned by the main window, loses its frame, menu, tabs and address bar, follows the cell when the window moves, resizes, minimizes or changes mode, and shows the page at the breakpoint's width scaled to the cell, as a Chromium view does. Every Firefox view renders at one factor (the smallest cell's); a changed factor restarts Firefox. Ctrl+Shift+Space V D shows them as windows of their own again, Ctrl+Shift+Space V V puts one back. Off (default): every such view is a window of its own beside the main window.
embed.label: Views in their cells

placement.description: Where a new Firefox or WebKit window goes: beside the main window, on monitor:<n> (1, 2, ...), or where it was last (remember). Further windows cascade.
placement.help: Where a new Firefox or WebKit window opens: beside the main window, on a given monitor (monitor:2), or where it was last (remember). Further windows cascade from there.
placement.label: Window placement

restartOnCrash.description: A Firefox or WebKit window whose engine crashed starts again by itself with its last page, at most three times in a row. A window you closed stays closed until you open it again.
restartOnCrash.help: A Firefox or WebKit window whose engine crashed starts again by itself with its last page, at most three times in a row. Off leaves it closed until you restart it from its cell. A window you closed by hand always stays closed until Open again.
restartOnCrash.label: Restart after a crash

scaleToCell.description: A Firefox or WebKit view in its cell shows its page at the breakpoint's width scaled to the cell, like a Chromium view. Off: the page at 100 %, cut to the cell. Nothing without "Views in their cells".
scaleToCell.help: With "Views in their cells" on, the page of a Firefox or WebKit view is scaled to its cell as a Chromium view's is: the breakpoint's width at the cell's width, the cell's height. WebKit renders at the cell's factor (its page then reports that factor as devicePixelRatio; screenshots keep the breakpoint's size); every Firefox view renders at the one factor of the profile, the smallest of their cells', and a changed factor restarts Firefox. Off: the page at 100 %, cut to the cell.
scaleToCell.label: Scale the page to the cell

showTiles.description: Show each external view's engine and status, with Show window and Restart, in its cell of the grid.
showTiles.help: Shows each external view's engine and status in its grid cell, with Show window and Restart. Off leaves the cell empty.
showTiles.label: Show external views in the grid

extraPrefs.description: Extra Firefox prefs written to the profile's user.js at every start (name to true, false, a number or text), for what Firefox cannot emulate per view - for example ui.prefersReducedMotion: 1. The remote agent's remote.* prefs are refused.
extraPrefs.help: Extra Firefox prefs written to the profile's user.js at every start, for what Firefox cannot emulate per view. Example: ui.prefersReducedMotion to 1. The remote agent's remote.* prefs are refused.
extraPrefs.label: Extra Firefox prefs

path.description: The Firefox executable. Empty: rBrowser finds the installed Firefox (the registry, then Program Files and the local app data).
path.help: The Firefox program rBrowser drives over WebDriver BiDi. Example: C:\Program Files\Mozilla Firefox\firefox.exe. Empty finds the installed Firefox: the registry's App Paths entry, the Mozilla Firefox folder under Program Files, Program Files (x86) and the local app data, the registry's uninstall entries, then the Firefox ESR, Firefox Developer Edition and Firefox Nightly folders; the field lists what was found.
path.label: Firefox path

profileDir.description: The folder of rBrowser's own Firefox profile, absolute or relative to rBrowser's local folder. Empty: a folder per project in rBrowser's local folder, never inside the project. A folder with someone else's data, or a link, is refused.
profileDir.help: The folder of rBrowser's own Firefox profile, absolute or relative to rBrowser's local folder. Empty creates one folder per project there, never inside the project. A folder holding someone else's profile, or a link, is refused.
profileDir.label: Profile folder

syncSource.description: A click in a Firefox window makes it the active view, and the other views follow what you do there.
syncSource.help: A click into a Firefox window makes it the active view and the other views follow what you do there. Off, Firefox windows only follow the others.
syncSource.label: Firefox leads the sync too

firefoxPath.description: The Firefox executable; found automatically when empty.
firefoxPath.label: Firefox path

lighthouseBrowserPath.description: The Chromium-based browser Lighthouse runs in. Empty finds one: Playwright's Chromium, then an installed Google Chrome or Microsoft Edge.
lighthouseBrowserPath.help: The Chromium-based browser the Lighthouse check starts headless for each run, as an absolute path. Example: C:\Program Files\Google\Chrome\Application\chrome.exe. Empty finds one itself: Playwright's Chromium, then an installed Google Chrome, then Microsoft Edge. Applies after the Node sidecar restarts.
lighthouseBrowserPath.label: Lighthouse browser

nodePath.description: A Node runtime of your own instead of the bundled one.
nodePath.help: A Node runtime of your own for the sidecar (WebKit, flows, Lighthouse) instead of the bundled one. Example: C:\Program Files\nodejs\node.exe. Empty uses the bundled runtime.
nodePath.label: Node runtime

nodeRpcTimeoutMs.description: How long a request to the Node sidecar (WebKit, flows, Lighthouse) waits for its answer before it is cancelled, in milliseconds.
nodeRpcTimeoutMs.help: How long a request to the Node sidecar waits for its answer, in milliseconds, before it is cancelled and reported. Raise it for a slow machine or a long Lighthouse run.
nodeRpcTimeoutMs.label: Node request timeout

playwrightBrowsersPath.description: The folder WebKit is downloaded to. Empty: %LOCALAPPDATA%\rBrowser\ms-playwright.
playwrightBrowsersPath.help: The folder Playwright downloads WebKit into. Example: D:\browsers to keep it off the system drive. Empty uses %LOCALAPPDATA%\rBrowser\ms-playwright.
playwrightBrowsersPath.label: Playwright browsers folder

enabled.description: Breakpoints on WebKit open in a WebKit window - Playwright's WebKit build, not Safari. Off, Chromium shows them.
enabled.help: Breakpoints with the WebKit engine open in a WebKit window, Playwright's build rather than Safari, downloaded on first use. Off shows those breakpoints in Chromium instead.
enabled.label: WebKit windows

syncSource.description: Clicks, keys and scrolling in a WebKit window are synced to the other views while it is the active view. Off, WebKit windows only follow.
syncSource.help: Clicks, keys and scrolling in a WebKit window are synced to the other views while it is the active view. Off, WebKit windows only follow.
syncSource.label: Sync from WebKit windows

breakpoints.description: The breakpoints compared when a comparison names none; empty compares every Chromium breakpoint.
breakpoints.help: The breakpoint ids a comparison runs over when the command names none; empty takes every Chromium breakpoint. Example: mobile, desktop.
breakpoints.label: Breakpoints

environments.description: The environments compared when a comparison names none; empty compares every environment.
environments.help: The environment ids a comparison runs over when the command names none; empty compares every environment of the project. Example: staging, production.
environments.label: Environments

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page, not only the viewport.
fullPage.help: Compare the whole scrolled page per environment, not only the viewport. Off is faster and avoids differences from pages of different length.
fullPage.label: Full page

maxDiffPercent.description: The share of differing pixels, in percent (0 to 100), up to which two environments still count as the same.
maxDiffPercent.help: The share of differing pixels, in percent (0 to 100), up to which two environments still count as the same. Example: 0.5 to ignore a changing banner. 0 flags every difference.
maxDiffPercent.label: Tolerated difference

parallel.description: How many shots are taken at the same time, each in its own hidden view (1 to 8).
parallel.help: How many shots a comparison takes at once, each in its own hidden view (1 to 8). Fewer is gentler on the servers compared.
parallel.label: Shots at once

threshold.description: How different two pixels may be and still count as equal, from 0 to 1; empty takes the visual regression threshold.
threshold.help: How different two pixels may be and still count as equal when environments are compared, from 0 to 1. Empty takes Capture > Visual regression > Colour tolerance.
threshold.label: Colour threshold

waitMs.description: A further pause before each screenshot, in milliseconds (0 to 30000), after the page loaded and the network went quiet.
waitMs.help: A further pause before each shot of a comparison, in milliseconds (0 to 30000), after the load and a quiet network, for animations that end late. Example: 500.
waitMs.label: Extra wait

environments.description: The environments (local, staging, ...) the toolbar switches between; each has an id, an origin and a border colour.
environments.help: The servers a site runs on, switched from the toolbar; bookmarks and paths follow the chosen one and the environment comparison diffs them. Example: id staging, url https://staging.example.com, colour #f59e0b.
environments.label: Environments

extensions.description: Browser extensions the project recommends; applied only in a trusted workspace.
extensions.help: Browser extensions the project recommends to the team: a Chrome Web Store id or URL, or an unpacked folder inside the project. Offered in a notice and loaded only in a trusted workspace, never by themselves.
extensions.label: Recommended extensions

arrowKeys.description: In focus mode, left and right arrow switch the breakpoint while the toolbar has the focus.
arrowKeys.help: In focus mode, the left and right arrow keys switch to the previous or next breakpoint while the toolbar has the focus. Off leaves the arrows to the page.
arrowKeys.label: Arrow keys switch breakpoints

keepFocus.description: A page loading in the focus view (each arrow key opens the next breakpoint's view) leaves the keyboard focus where it is, so the toolbar's next arrow key steps again. Off: the view takes the focus, as a page does after a navigation.
keepFocus.help: In focus mode every arrow key opens the next breakpoint's view, and the page loading there would take the keyboard focus. On (the default) refuses that, so you can step through the breakpoints with one click into the toolbar; off lets the new view take the focus as after a navigation.
keepFocus.label: Keep the keyboard focus on arrow keys

react.description: React DevTools (react-devtools-inline): components, props, hooks and the profiler in a panel. auto offers the panel once a page runs React and puts the hook into the view's next document (reload the view once); on puts the hook into every page before its scripts, so the panel connects without a reload; off injects and offers nothing.
react.help: How the React DevTools panel is offered. auto (the default) offers it once a page runs React and injects the hook into the view's next document, so reload once; on injects the hook into every page before its scripts, so the panel connects without a reload; off injects and offers nothing.
react.label: React DevTools

vue.description: Vue DevTools (Vue 3, @vue/devtools-kit): components, props and state in a panel. auto offers the panel once a page runs Vue and puts the hook into the view's next document (reload the view once); on puts the hook into every page before its scripts; off injects and offers nothing. A production build shows components only when built with __VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__.
vue.help: How the Vue DevTools panel is offered. auto (the default) offers it once a page runs Vue and injects the hook into the view's next document, so reload once; on injects the hook into every page before its scripts; off injects and offers nothing. Production builds need __VUE_PROD_DEVTOOLS__.
vue.label: Vue DevTools

defaultZoom.description: The zoom of the cells rBrowser lays out itself (no cells in the config, focus mode): fit to the cell, or a factor from 0.25 to 1.
defaultZoom.help: The zoom of cells rBrowser lays out itself (no cells in the config, focus mode): fit scales a view into its cell, a factor from 0.25 to 1 keeps a fixed scale. Example: 0.5.
defaultZoom.label: Default cell zoom

fitToWindow.description: When the layout changes (a layout preset, focus mode, the project opening or its config changing), views zoomed by hand go back to their cell's zoom. Off, they keep their zoom.
fitToWindow.help: When the layout changes (a preset, focus mode, the project opening, a config change), views zoomed by hand return to their cell's zoom. Off keeps your hand zoom through layout changes.
fitToWindow.label: Reset hand zoom on layout change

layout.description: Columns, rows, gap and the cells of the grid when no preset overrides it.
layout.help: The grid used when no preset is active: columns, rows, the gap between views in pixels and which breakpoint sits in which cell. Example: 2 columns, 1 row, gap 8.
layout.label: Grid

horizontalHeight.description: The views' height in the horizontal layout when the preset sets none: fit to the window, or a height in DIP.
horizontalHeight.help: The views' height in the horizontal strip when the preset sets none: fit uses the window's height, a number is a height in DIP. Example: 900.
horizontalHeight.label: Horizontal row height

middleButtonPan.description: Canvas: the middle mouse button held and dragged pans the canvas, as Space + drag does - over a view, a label or a breakpoint bar too; the page's autoscroll does not start there. A middle click without dragging still reaches the page. Off gives the middle button back to the pages.
middleButtonPan.help: Hold the middle mouse button anywhere on the canvas and drag to pan it, also when the pointer starts on a view; Escape puts the canvas back. A middle click without dragging still reaches the page (a link opens in the background). Off gives the middle button back to the pages; Space + drag and dragging the empty canvas still pan.
middleButtonPan.label: Pan with the middle mouse button

minimap.description: Shows every view of the canvas and the visible part in the toolbar; a click centres the canvas there.
minimap.help: Shows a small map of the whole canvas and the visible part in the toolbar; a click centres the canvas there, a drag moves a view. Off hides it.
minimap.label: Canvas minimap

minimapPosition.description: At the end or the start of the toolbar.
minimapPosition.help: Where the canvas minimap sits in the toolbar: at the end (right) or the start (left).
minimapPosition.label: Minimap position

savePresetTo.description: Where "Save layout as preset" writes when it is not told: local (config.local.json, only you) or project (config.json, shared with the team).
savePresetTo.help: Where Save layout as preset writes when not told: local keeps the preset in config.local.json for you alone, project writes config.json for the whole team.
savePresetTo.label: Save layout presets to

showPartialViews.description: Canvas: a view that reaches past the edge of the grid area shows the part of its page that lies inside; only a view wholly outside is hidden and paused. Off: a view is hidden as soon as any part of it leaves the area.
showPartialViews.help: On the canvas a view that reaches past the edge of the window shows the part of its page that is still inside; a view wholly outside is hidden and paused. Off hides a view as soon as any part of it leaves the grid area, so only its frame and label remain.
showPartialViews.label: Show views that reach past the edge

snap.description: A moved view snaps to this grid in DIP (0 for none) and to the edges of views closer than it, unless the canvas preset sets its own snap.
snap.help: The grid a moved view snaps to on the canvas, in DIP, and the distance at which it snaps to another view's edge. 0 moves freely. A canvas preset can set its own.
snap.label: Canvas snap grid

spacePan.description: Holding Space turns any drag on the canvas - on a view's label too - into panning. A drag on the empty canvas always pans; Space typed into a page stays a space.
spacePan.help: Holding Space turns any drag on the canvas, on a view's label too, into panning. Dragging the empty canvas always pans; Space typed into a page stays a space. Off pans only on the empty canvas.
spacePan.label: Pan with Space + drag

splitStep.description: How far one keyboard step moves the split divider, as a share of the area (0.01 to 0.25).
splitStep.help: How far one keyboard press moves the split divider, as a share of the area (0.01 to 0.25). 0.05 moves five percent per press.
splitStep.label: Divider keyboard step

wheelZoom.description: Canvas: Ctrl + mouse wheel over the canvas - the free area, a view's label or its breakpoint bar - zooms the canvas around the pointer; the views grow and shrink with it. Off: the wheel does nothing there. Over a view the page zooms, as in every layout. rBrowser's own toolbar and status bar never zoom.
wheelZoom.help: Hold Ctrl and turn the mouse wheel over the free canvas or a view's label to zoom the canvas around the pointer, between 5 % and 100 %; the views are scaled with it. Over a view the wheel zooms that page. Off leaves the canvas zoom to Zoom to fit and the layout commands.
wheelZoom.label: Zoom the canvas with Ctrl + wheel

layouts.description: Named layouts (grid or focus mode) and the one used at start.
layouts.help: Named arrangements of the grid you switch between (Ctrl+Shift+Space, L) and the one the project opens with. Example: a review preset with four columns, a focus preset with one view.
layouts.label: Layout presets

crashDumpsInBundle.description: How many of the newest crash dumps the diagnostics ZIP includes. 0 includes none. Dumps can hold page content.
crashDumpsInBundle.help: How many of the newest crash dumps the diagnostics ZIP includes; 0 includes none. A dump can hold page content, so lower it before sharing the ZIP outside the team.
crashDumpsInBundle.label: Crash dumps in the diagnostics ZIP

level.description: How much rBrowser writes to its log. RUST_LOG, when set, takes precedence.
level.help: How much rBrowser writes to its log: error, warn, info, debug or trace. Use debug for a diagnostics ZIP; trace is very verbose. The environment variable RUST_LOG, when set, wins.
level.label: Log level

maxFileSizeMb.description: The size at which the log file is rotated.
maxFileSizeMb.help: The size at which the log file is rotated into a numbered older file, in MB. Example: 10.
maxFileSizeMb.label: Log file size

maxFiles.description: How many log files are kept, the current one included. Older ones are deleted.
maxFiles.help: How many log files are kept, the current one included; older rotated files are deleted. Example: 5 keeps about 50 MB with the default size.
maxFiles.label: Log files kept

allowEvaluate.description: Let MCP agents run JavaScript in the pages.
allowEvaluate.help: Lets MCP agents run JavaScript in the pages through the evaluate tool. Keep it off unless an agent needs it: a page script runs with the page's rights.
allowEvaluate.label: Allow evaluate

consoleLogLimit.description: How many console messages rBrowser keeps per view for MCP agents (console_logs).
consoleLogLimit.help: How many console messages rBrowser keeps per view for the console_logs tool; older ones drop out. Raise it for noisy pages.
consoleLogLimit.label: Console messages kept

enabled.description: Let AI agents control rBrowser over the Model Context Protocol.
enabled.help: Starts the MCP server on 127.0.0.1 so AI agents can control rBrowser through the Model Context Protocol, protected by a token. Off starts no server and rbrowser mcp cannot connect.
enabled.label: MCP server

errorLimit.description: How many uncaught page errors rBrowser keeps per view for MCP agents (errors).
errorLimit.help: How many uncaught page errors rBrowser keeps per view for the errors tool; older ones drop out.
errorLimit.label: Page errors kept

maxAnswerBytes.description: The largest answer of evaluate and snapshot, in bytes. Longer answers are cut.
maxAnswerBytes.help: The largest answer of evaluate and snapshot, in bytes; longer answers are cut and marked. Example: 262144 for 256 KiB. Lower it to keep an agent's context small.
maxAnswerBytes.label: Largest answer

navigationTimeoutMs.description: How long MCP waits for each view, in milliseconds: the final URL of navigate, reload, back and forward, the input of click, type, hover and press_key, and the work of sync_set.
navigationTimeoutMs.help: How long MCP waits per view for the result of navigate, reload, back, forward, click, type, hover, press_key and sync_set, in milliseconds, before it answers with a timeout. Raise it for slow pages.
navigationTimeoutMs.label: Navigation wait

networkRequestLimit.description: How many network requests rBrowser keeps per view for MCP agents (network_requests). Headers and bodies are never kept.
networkRequestLimit.help: How many network requests rBrowser keeps per view for the network_requests tool; headers and bodies are never kept. Raise it for pages that load many assets.
networkRequestLimit.label: Network requests kept

notifyOnSettingChange.description: Show a notice in rBrowser whenever an MCP agent changes a setting. Every change is written to the log either way.
notifyOnSettingChange.help: Shows a notice in rBrowser whenever an MCP agent changes a setting, so a change never goes unnoticed. Every change is written to the log either way.
notifyOnSettingChange.label: Notify on MCP setting changes

port.description: A fixed port on 127.0.0.1 for the MCP server. Empty picks a free port at every start.
port.help: A fixed port on 127.0.0.1 for the MCP server, so a client config can name it. Example: 7420. Empty picks a free port at every start and writes it to the instance file.
port.label: Port

stdioAutoStart.description: When an MCP client starts rbrowser mcp and the project's rBrowser is not running, start it in the background. The MCP server must be on.
stdioAutoStart.help: When an MCP client runs rbrowser mcp and the project's rBrowser is not running, start it in the background. Needs the MCP server on. Off makes the client wait for a running rBrowser.
stdioAutoStart.label: Start rBrowser for MCP clients

hostResolverRules.description: Chromium host resolver rules that map host names to other addresses.
hostResolverRules.help: Chromium's host resolver rules, which map host names to other addresses without touching the hosts file. Example: MAP www.example.com 127.0.0.1 to test production URLs against a local server.
hostResolverRules.label: Host resolver rules

ignoreCertificateErrors.description: Accept invalid TLS certificates. Only in config.local.json, never shared with the team.
ignoreCertificateErrors.help: Accepts invalid or self-signed TLS certificates in every view, for local HTTPS servers. Only in config.local.json, never shared with the team, and only in a trusted workspace.
ignoreCertificateErrors.label: Ignore certificate errors

proxy.description: A proxy server (host:port) or a PAC URL. Only in config.local.json.
proxy.help: A proxy every view connects through, as host:port, or a PAC URL. Example: 127.0.0.1:8080 to route the views through a debugging proxy. Only in config.local.json.
proxy.label: Proxy

enabled.description: Gives every view's page window.__rbrowser with the view's label, size, index, engine, emulation and the message bus. A change applies from the next page load.
enabled.help: Gives every page window.__rbrowser with the view's label, size, index, engine and emulation and the message bus, for debugging and for project scripts. Off hides rBrowser from the page. Applies from the next load.
enabled.label: Page API

uaSuffix.description: Ends every view's user agent, an emulated one included, in rBrowser/<version>, so servers and analytics can tell rBrowser apart.
uaSuffix.help: Appends rBrowser/<version> to every view's user agent, an emulated one included, so servers and analytics can tell rBrowser traffic apart. Off sends the plain user agent.
uaSuffix.label: User-agent suffix

prefixes.description: In the command palette, > lists only commands, @ only views and # only settings. Off: these characters are searched as text.
prefixes.help: In the command palette, > lists only commands, @ only views and # only settings. Off searches these characters as text.
prefixes.label: Search prefixes

recentCount.description: How many recently used entries the command palette lists first; 0 keeps no history.
recentCount.help: How many recently used entries the command palette lists first, before the search; 0 keeps no history. Example: 8.
recentCount.label: Recent entries

showDescriptions.description: The command palette shows the description of the selected entry: a command's id, a setting's text, a view's address.
showDescriptions.help: The command palette shows the description of the selected entry: a command's id, a setting's text, a view's address. Off shows titles only.
showDescriptions.label: Show descriptions

closeTo.description: What closing the plugin panels does: rail folds them to the narrow icon rail beside the views, hidden hides them completely.
closeTo.help: Applies to the X in the panels' header, to Close the plugin panels (Ctrl+Shift+Space, P, X) and to closing the panels' own window. rail (the default) folds them to the icon rail - a click on an icon opens that panel again; the window's panels come back docked as the rail. hidden removes them until a panel is opened again or the panels' switch in the toolbar is clicked. Hide the panels in the Dock menu hides them whatever this says.
closeTo.label: Closing the panels

dock.description: Where the plugin panels open: floating in a window of their own, or docked left, right or below the views, which make room.
dock.help: Where the plugin panels (Network, Console, Storage and the others) open. right (the default), left, bottom: docked in the main window below the toolbar; the views move together and nothing covers them; closed, the panels fold to their icon rail. floating: a window of their own. The Dock menu in the panels' header and the commands Leader P Left, P Right, P Down and P Up set it.
dock.label: Plugin panels position

dockAtStart.description: How the docked plugin panels start: rail as the narrow icon rail beside the views, hidden, or last as they were left.
dockAtStart.help: rail (the default) starts the docked panels folded to the icon rail - the icons of every panel, Findings first, an expand button on top - so the views have their room from the start and never jump. hidden starts without them. last starts them as they were left: open, the rail or hidden. Panels left in their own window start as the rail on the right; the window never opens by itself.
dockAtStart.label: Plugin panels at the start

bottom.description: The height of the plugin panels docked below the views, in pixels. Drag the bar between panels and views to change it.
bottom.help: The height of the plugin panels docked below the views, in pixels. Dragging the bar between the panels and the views changes it; the views keep at least a quarter of the window.
bottom.label: Docked panels height (below)

left.description: The width of the plugin panels docked left of the views, in pixels. Drag the bar between panels and views to change it.
left.help: The width of the plugin panels docked left of the views, in pixels. Dragging the bar between the panels and the views changes it; the views keep at least a quarter of the window.
left.label: Docked panels width (left)

right.description: The width of the plugin panels docked right of the views, in pixels. Drag the bar between panels and views to change it.
right.help: The width of the plugin panels docked right of the views, in pixels. Dragging the bar between the panels and the views changes it; the views keep at least a quarter of the window.
right.label: Docked panels width (right)

dockState.description: The docked plugin panels now: open at their size, rail folded to the narrow icon rail so the views get the room, or hidden.
dockState.help: open shows the docked panels at their size. rail folds them to the icon rail - beside the views a column of icons, below them a row - and the views get the room; a click on an icon, the expand button, the panels' switch in the toolbar or Ctrl+Shift+Space, P, Z opens them again. A panel a command or a check opens while they are folded stays folded and is marked in the rail. hidden removes them; a panel opened by a command brings the rail back. The state survives a restart unless Plugin panels at the start says otherwise.
dockState.label: Docked plugin panels

sidebar.description: The plugin panels' side bar: icons with titles (expanded), or icons only with the title as a tooltip.
sidebar.help: expanded (the default) lists every panel with its icon and title; icons shows only the icons, with the title as a tooltip, and leaves the panel more room. The button at the bottom of the side bar switches it. It applies to the panels' own window and to the docked panels; a narrow dock shows icons only either way.
sidebar.label: Panels side bar

inactiveFps.description: Visible views that are not the active one run their pages slowed to about this many frames per second of work (CPU throttling, 60 divided by the value). 0 or 60 leaves them at full speed. Sync still reaches them, a little later.
inactiveFps.help: Slows the pages of visible views that are not the active one to about this many frames per second of work (CPU throttling, 60 divided by the value), to keep eight views fluid. 0 or 60 is full speed.
inactiveFps.label: Frame budget of inactive views

memoryWarningMb.description: Shows a warning once when rBrowser's processes together use more private memory than this many MB. 0 turns the warning off.
memoryWarningMb.help: Shows a warning once when rBrowser's processes together use more private memory than this many MB, so you can close views before Windows swaps. 0 turns the warning off.
memoryWarningMb.label: Memory warning threshold

throttleHidden.description: A view with no area on screen stops painting and runs its timers slowly. It still follows navigation and scrolling, and shows the leader's current page and scroll position when it is visible again. Off, hidden views keep rendering.
throttleHidden.help: A view with no area on screen stops painting and runs its timers slowly, saving CPU; it still follows navigation and scrolling and catches up when shown. Off keeps hidden views rendering.
throttleHidden.label: Throttle hidden views

autoUpdate.description: Install plugin updates by themselves when they need no new permission.
autoUpdate.help: When the update check finds a newer version of a plugin that ships with rBrowser or came from the catalog, signed by the same key and asking for nothing more, it is installed by itself and loads at the next start. An update that asks for more waits in the catalog for your click.
autoUpdate.label: Update plugins automatically

checkOnStart.description: Look for updates of the plugins from the catalog at every start.
checkOnStart.help: At every start rBrowser fetches the signed indexes of the official catalog and your repositories and says in the status bar when a plugin installed from the catalog has an update. Nothing is installed by itself.
checkOnStart.label: Check for plugin updates at start

missingNotice.description: Say in the status bar when the project uses a plugin that is not installed.
missingNotice.help: When the project's .rbrowser/config.json has settings of a plugin that is not installed, the status bar says which, with a button to the plugin catalog. Off, nothing is said.
missingNotice.label: Name missing project plugins

preferRepository.description: Install a chosen plugin from the official catalog when it has a newer version.
preferRepository.help: Every plugin rBrowser ships is in the package. On, a plugin you choose comes from the official catalog when it offers a newer version than the shipped one, signed by the same key and asking for nothing more; without a network it comes from the package. Off, every chosen plugin comes from the package and nothing reaches the network.
preferRepository.label: Prefer the plugin catalog

repositories.description: Repositories besides the official catalog: the address of the index and its public key.
repositories.help: Each repository is the https address of its rbrowser-plugin-index.json and the Ed25519 public key (base64) its index is signed with. The catalog lists its plugins beside the official ones; a plugin from it is still verified and installs only after you confirmed its capabilities.
repositories.label: Plugin repositories

compileCache.description: Store compiled plugin code so the next start is faster.
compileCache.help: Stores compiled plugin code on disk so the next start is faster. Off compiles every plugin at every start.
compileCache.label: Keep compiled plugins

crashLimit.description: How many failures within five minutes pause a plugin.
crashLimit.help: How many failures within five minutes pause a plugin until you resume it, so a broken plugin cannot take rBrowser down. Example: 3.
crashLimit.label: Failures before pausing

developmentMode.description: Load unsigned plugins. Every such plugin is marked as unsigned.
developmentMode.help: Loads unsigned plugins, for developing your own; every such plugin is marked unsigned. Off refuses them.
developmentMode.label: Development mode

disabled.description: Plugins that stay installed but do not load. Their settings are kept.
disabled.help: Plugin ids that stay installed but are not loaded; their settings are kept. Example: image-overlay, snippets. Enable them again here or in the plugins panel.
disabled.label: Disabled plugins

lighthouseAnyUrl.description: Let plugins run Lighthouse on addresses outside the sites the views show.
lighthouseAnyUrl.help: Off, a Lighthouse run a plugin starts is held to the sites the views show, so it cannot read local or network pages through the report. Only you can switch it on; MCP cannot.
lighthouseAnyUrl.label: Lighthouse on any address

pageScriptsDisabled.description: Plugins whose scripts do not run in the pages of the views. Switching one on again is only possible here, not over MCP.
pageScriptsDisabled.help: Plugin ids whose scripts do not run inside the pages of the views (overlays, inspectors). Switching a script on again is only possible here, never over MCP.
pageScriptsDisabled.label: Page scripts switched off

panelMessageMaxBytes.description: The largest message between a plugin panel and rBrowser, in bytes: a call, its answer, an event. A larger answer is refused and the panel names this setting.
panelMessageMaxBytes.help: The largest message between a plugin panel and rBrowser, in bytes, in either direction: a call's arguments, its answer, an event. A larger one is refused and the panel names this setting. Example: 4194304 for 4 MiB, the default; from 65536 (64 KiB) to 16777216 (16 MiB). The scripts plugins run in the pages of the views keep their own 64 KiB.
panelMessageMaxBytes.label: Panel message limit

panelsHidden.description: Plugins whose panels the plugin panels window does not offer.
panelsHidden.help: Plugin ids whose panels the plugin panels window does not offer, to keep the list short. The plugins keep running.
panelsHidden.label: Panels hidden

showBundled.description: List the plugins that ship with rBrowser beside the ones you installed.
showBundled.help: Shows the plugins that ship with rBrowser in Settings > Plugins. Off lists only the plugins you installed and the project's; the bundled ones keep running.
showBundled.label: Show bundled plugins

trustedKeys.description: Keys you confirmed for plugins from other publishers.
trustedKeys.help: Signing keys you confirmed for plugins from other publishers (key id, public key, fingerprint). A plugin signed by one of them installs without a new trust question.
trustedKeys.label: Trusted signing keys

fitToScreen.description: A window larger than the screen is cut to it and the page shown at a smaller zoom, named in the window title. Off, the window keeps the real size beyond the screen.
fitToScreen.help: A popped-out window larger than the screen is cut to the screen and the page shown at a smaller zoom, named in the title. Off keeps the real size, partly off screen.
fitToScreen.label: Fit the window to the screen

keepPlaceholder.description: The grid keeps the cell of a popped-out view with a placeholder; a click brings the window to the front. Off, the other views close the gap.
keepPlaceholder.help: The grid keeps the cell of a popped-out view with a placeholder; a click on it brings the window to the front. Off closes the gap and the other views grow.
keepPlaceholder.label: Keep a placeholder in the grid

rememberBounds.description: Each breakpoint's window opens where and as large as it was last closed.
rememberBounds.help: Each breakpoint's popped-out window opens where and as large as it was last closed. Off opens it beside the main window every time.
rememberBounds.label: Remember the window's place and size

enabled.description: Let real devices in the LAN join the sync after pairing with a QR code. Off, the portal cannot be started. Only a person starts it; MCP cannot.
enabled.help: Lets real phones and tablets in the LAN join the sync after pairing with a QR code. Off, the portal cannot be started. Only a person starts it; MCP cannot.
enabled.label: Portal

interface.description: The IPv4 address of the network interface the portal listens on. Empty uses the interface of the default route, but only when its address is a private LAN address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x, 169.254.x, 100.64-127.x); a public or VPN address refuses to start, so set the interface here. The portal never listens on every interface.
interface.help: The IPv4 address of the network interface the portal listens on. Empty takes the default route's interface when it is a private LAN address; a public or VPN address refuses to start. Example: 192.168.1.20.
interface.label: Portal interface

maxDevices.description: How many devices may be paired with the portal at once.
maxDevices.help: How many devices may be paired with the portal at the same time; a further pairing is refused until one is removed.
maxDevices.label: Most devices

offerAssetOrigins.description: When a portal page loads from a local address the shown environment does not list in its asset origins, the status bar offers to add it. Off, only the log names the address.
offerAssetOrigins.help: When a page on a device loads images, styles or scripts from a local address the portal does not forward (http://localhost:5173), the status bar offers to add it to the environment's asset origins; your click writes the project config. Off, only the log names the address.
offerAssetOrigins.label: Offer to add asset origins

pairingTtlSec.description: How long the pairing code in the QR code stays valid, in seconds. Each code works once.
pairingTtlSec.help: How long a pairing code in the QR code stays valid, in seconds; each code works once. Lower it to limit the window in which someone else could scan it.
pairingTtlSec.label: Pairing code lifetime

port.description: A fixed port for the portal; a random free port when empty. A fixed port needs only one Windows firewall rule.
port.help: A fixed port for the portal, so one Windows firewall rule suffices. Example: 7430. Empty picks a free port at every start.
port.label: Portal port

recentProjects.description: The projects opened last, newest first.
recentProjects.help: The projects opened last, newest first, as the Open recent menu lists them. Remove an entry to forget a project; MCP cannot add one.
recentProjects.label: Recent projects

debounceMs.description: How long to wait after the last change before reloading, in milliseconds.
debounceMs.help: How long to wait after the last file change before reloading, in milliseconds, so a build that writes many files reloads once. Raise it to 500 or more for slow builds.
debounceMs.label: Reload delay

ignore.description: Glob patterns whose changes never reload.
ignore.help: Glob patterns whose changes never trigger a reload, such as build output or logs. Example: node_modules/**, dist/**, **/*.log.
ignore.label: Ignored files

intervalPauseSec.description: How long input in a view pauses the interval reload, in seconds.
intervalPauseSec.help: How long typing or clicking in a view pauses the interval reload, in seconds, so a reload does not interrupt what you do. Example: 10.
intervalPauseSec.label: Interval pause after input

intervalSec.description: Reload every view this often, in seconds, for pages no file watch can see (a staging server). 0 switches it off; an environment can set its own.
intervalSec.help: Reloads every view this often, in seconds, for pages no file watch can see, such as a staging server. Example: 30. 0 switches it off; an environment can set its own interval.
intervalSec.label: Interval reload

mode.description: On change, swap stylesheets and images in place and reload for everything else (auto), always reload the whole page (full), or reload only on command (manual).
mode.help: What a change does: auto swaps stylesheets and images in place and reloads for anything else, full always reloads the whole page, manual reloads only on command (Ctrl+Shift+Space, R).
mode.label: Reload mode

pollIntervalMs.description: How often polling looks for changes, in milliseconds (at least 250).
pollIntervalMs.help: How often polling looks for changed files, in milliseconds (at least 250). Lower is quicker to reload, higher is gentler on the disk.
pollIntervalMs.label: Polling interval

pollingFallback.description: Check files for changes periodically instead of relying on file system events.
pollingFallback.help: Checks watched files for changes periodically instead of relying on file system events, for network drives and some WSL setups where events do not arrive. Off uses events only.
