pollingFallback.label: Polling fallback

respectHmr.description: Leave pages with their own hot module replacement (Vite, webpack) to their dev server instead of reloading them on change.
respectHmr.help: Pages with their own hot module replacement (Vite, webpack dev server) are left to it instead of being reloaded by the watcher, so component state survives. Off reloads them anyway.
respectHmr.label: Respect the dev server's HMR

watch.description: Glob patterns, relative to the project, whose changes reload the views.
watch.help: Glob patterns, relative to the project, whose changes reload the views, so a saved file shows at every breakpoint at once. Example: src/**/*.css, src/**/*.js, public/**. Empty watches nothing.
watch.label: Watched files

cpuWarnPercent.description: A view whose main thread is busier than this share for five seconds is marked in its label and logged.
cpuWarnPercent.help: A view whose main thread is busier than this share, in percent, for five seconds is marked in its label and noted in the log. Lower it to spot busy pages sooner.
cpuWarnPercent.label: CPU warning

enabled.description: Read each Chromium view's CPU share and JS memory every two seconds and show them in its label.
enabled.help: Reads each Chromium view's CPU share and JS memory every two seconds and shows them in its label, so a heavy page stands out. Off saves the sampling.
enabled.label: Show resources

ramWarnMb.description: A view whose JS memory is above this many MB is marked in its label and logged.
ramWarnMb.help: A view whose JS heap is above this many MB is marked in its label and noted in the log. Example: 500. Raise it for pages that legitimately hold much data.
ramWarnMb.label: Memory warning

seo.description: Settings of the SEO check: expected locales and the size of the crawl.
seo.help: The SEO plugin's project keys: the hreflang locales the site must offer and how many pages a crawl checks. Example: locales de, en-GB; maxPages 10. The rules themselves are under the SEO plugin.
seo.label: SEO check

sessionColors.description: The badge colour of each named session as #rrggbb; a session without one gets a colour of its own. "default" shows no badge.
sessionColors.help: The badge colour each session shows in a view's label, so you see at a glance which login a view holds. Example: admin to #d946ef. A session without an entry gets a colour of its own.
sessionColors.label: Session colours

sessions.description: Named cookie and storage partitions; "default" always exists and is shared by every Chromium view without one.
sessions.help: Named cookie and storage partitions, so one view can be logged in as an admin and another as a visitor. A breakpoint names its session; default is always there. Example: admin, visitor.
sessions.label: Sessions

persistSessionCookies.description: Keep session cookies (logins without an expiry date) on disk, so you stay signed in after a restart, in every session. Off, they end when rBrowser closes, as in a browser. Takes effect at the next start.
persistSessionCookies.help: Keeps session cookies (logins without an expiry) on disk, so every session stays signed in after a restart. Off ends them when rBrowser closes, as a browser does. Applies at the next start.
persistSessionCookies.label: Keep session cookies

jsonHighlight.description: The JSON view of the settings window colours keys, strings, numbers, booleans, null and punctuation.
jsonHighlight.help: Colours the JSON view (Show JSON) so keys, strings, numbers, true/false, null and brackets stand apart, in both themes. Off shows the JSON in one colour. Copy delivers plain JSON either way.
jsonHighlight.label: JSON view syntax colours

sectionTabs.description: A category with more than one section shows one section per tab.
sectionTabs.help: Splits a long category (Layout, Engines, Capture) into one tab per section, so you see one section at a time. The search, Only changed and a link to a setting still reach every tab. Off shows every section of a category on one page.
sectionTabs.label: Sections as tabs

showKeys.description: Print each setting's key (updates.channel) under its title.
showKeys.help: The key is what the config file, MCP's settings_set and a colleague's message use. Off, it stays in the title's tooltip and behind the copy button that appears when you point at a setting; the search finds settings by key either way.
showKeys.label: Show setting keys

bindings.description: Your bindings per command; they replace the defaults. An empty list unbinds a command.
bindings.help: Your keyboard shortcuts per command, replacing the defaults; an empty list unbinds a command. Edit them in Settings > Keyboard Shortcuts, which refuses reserved combinations.
bindings.label: Keyboard shortcuts

disableInDevtools.description: rBrowser's shortcuts do not fire while the DevTools panel has focus, so DevTools' own shortcuts keep working.
disableInDevtools.help: rBrowser's shortcuts do not fire while the DevTools panel has the focus, so DevTools' own shortcuts (Ctrl+F, Ctrl+Shift+C) keep working. Off lets rBrowser's shortcuts win there.
disableInDevtools.label: Off while DevTools have focus

leaderTimeoutMs.description: How long, in milliseconds, the leader Ctrl+Shift+Space waits for the next key; 0 (the default) waits until Esc or a key.
leaderTimeoutMs.help: How long the leader key Ctrl+Shift+Space waits for the next key of a chord, in milliseconds, before the which-key bar closes. Example: 4000.
leaderTimeoutMs.label: Leader timeout

autoScroll.description: Scroll each page to its end and back before the screenshot, so lazy-loaded content is there.
autoScroll.help: Scroll each page to its end and back before the screenshot, so lazy-loaded images and sections have appeared. Off leaves lazy content unloaded.
autoScroll.label: Scroll for lazy content

delayMs.description: A further pause before each screenshot, in milliseconds (0 to 30000).
delayMs.help: A further pause before each screenshot, in milliseconds (0 to 30000), for animations that end after the load. Example: 1000.
delayMs.label: Extra delay

exclude.description: Leave out the pages matching one of these patterns (glob or re:).
exclude.help: Leave out pages matching one of these patterns, as a glob or re:. Example: /tag/**, re:\?page=\d+ to skip tag and pagination pages.
exclude.label: Exclude patterns

fullPage.description: Capture the whole page, not only the viewport.
fullPage.help: Capture the whole scrolled page of each sitemap entry, not only the viewport. Off is faster and gives uniform images.
fullPage.label: Full page

hideSelectors.description: Deprecated, kept so older configs work: more elements to hide before each capture, as CSS selectors. Use Settings > Capture > Cookie-banner hiding > More elements to hide (capture.hideSelectors) instead; these join that list.
hideSelectors.help: Deprecated: extra CSS selectors hidden before each sitemap capture. Use Capture > Cookie banners > More elements to hide instead; entries here still join that list.
hideSelectors.label: Cookie banners to hide (deprecated)

hostIntervalMs.description: The least time between two page loads on one host, in milliseconds (0 to 60000), so a site is not flooded.
hostIntervalMs.help: The least time between two page loads on one host, in milliseconds (0 to 60000), so a capture does not flood a production server. Example: 1000 for one page per second.
hostIntervalMs.label: Pause per host

include.description: Capture only the pages matching one of these patterns: a glob over the path (/blog/**) or a regular expression after re:. Empty takes every page.
include.help: Capture only pages matching one of these patterns: a glob over the path (/blog/**) or a regular expression after re: (re:^/docs/v2). Empty captures every page of the sitemap.
include.label: Include patterns

maxDepth.description: How deep sitemap indexes may nest (0 to 5).
maxDepth.help: How deep nested sitemap indexes are followed (0 to 5); 0 reads only the sitemap named. Raise it for sites whose index points to indexes.
maxDepth.label: Sitemap index depth

maxPages.description: At most this many pages per run; 0 takes all.
maxPages.help: At most this many pages per run, for a quick sample of a large site. Example: 50. 0 takes every page the include and exclude patterns leave.
maxPages.label: Most pages

maxSitemapMib.description: The largest sitemap read, unpacked, in MiB (1 to 50).
maxSitemapMib.help: The largest sitemap file read, unpacked, in MiB (1 to 50); a larger one is skipped with a notice, so a broken sitemap cannot exhaust memory.
maxSitemapMib.label: Largest sitemap

maxUrls.description: The most page URLs read from the sitemaps (1 to 200000).
maxUrls.help: The most page URLs read from all sitemaps of a run (1 to 200000); the rest are ignored. Lower it for a sample of a huge site.
maxUrls.label: Most sitemap URLs

parallel.description: How many pages are captured at the same time, each in its own hidden view (1 to 8).
parallel.help: How many pages a sitemap capture takes at once, each in its own hidden view (1 to 8). More is faster; fewer is gentler on the server and the machine.
parallel.label: Pages at once

respectRobots.description: Leave out the pages the site's robots.txt disallows.
respectRobots.help: Leave out pages the site's robots.txt disallows, as a crawler would. Off captures them anyway, for a staging site that blocks every crawler.
respectRobots.label: Respect robots.txt

retries.description: How often a failed page is tried again in a run (0 to 5); a resumed run tries the failed ones again.
retries.help: How often a failed page is tried again within a run (0 to 5). A resumed run tries the failed ones again either way.
retries.label: Retries

timeoutSec.description: The longest one page may take from loading to its screenshot, in seconds (5 to 300).
timeoutSec.help: The longest a page may take from loading to its screenshot, in seconds (5 to 300); a slower page counts as failed and is retried. Raise it for heavy pages.
timeoutSec.label: Page timeout

waitNetworkIdle.description: Wait until the page has made no request for a moment after its load (at most 10 seconds).
waitNetworkIdle.help: Wait after each page's load until no request has been made for a moment (at most 10 seconds), so lazy content and fonts are there before the screenshot. Off captures right after the load.
waitNetworkIdle.label: Wait for network idle

waitSelector.description: A CSS selector the page must show before its screenshot; empty for none.
waitSelector.help: A CSS selector each page must show before its screenshot, for pages that render after a script. Example: main.loaded. Empty waits for nothing in particular.
waitSelector.label: Wait for a selector

startUrl.description: The URL every view loads when the project opens: an absolute http or https URL.
startUrl.help: Where every view starts when the project opens, so the team lands on the same page. Example: http://localhost:3000/. Empty leaves the views blank until you enter an address.
startUrl.label: Start URL

focusOnOpen.description: The window comes to the front when a project opens or another call hands it a URL.
focusOnOpen.help: The window comes to the front when a project opens or another rBrowser call hands it a URL. Off leaves the window where it is, for scripted openings.
focusOnOpen.label: Take the focus when opening

openLastProject.description: Started without a project, open the most recent one.
openLastProject.help: Started without a project, rBrowser opens the most recent one by itself. Off starts with the project chooser.
openLastProject.label: Open the last project

activateOnFocus.description: A click into a view makes it the active view, whose actions the other views follow. Off by default: a click on a view's label makes it active.
activateOnFocus.help: Whether a click into a page makes that view the active one the others follow. Off, only a click on a view's label changes the active view, so a click never changes who leads by accident.
activateOnFocus.label: A click into a view makes it active

click.description: Clicks are replayed in the other views.
click.help: A click in the active view is replayed at the same element in the other views, so menus and buttons open everywhere at once. Off, clicks stay in the view you clicked.
click.label: Sync clicks

contextMenu.description: Right clicks are replayed in the other views, so a page's own context menu opens there too. Off by default, because the browser's menu would open in every view at once.
contextMenu.help: Whether a right click is replayed in the other views, so a page's own context menu opens there too. Leave it off unless the page draws its own menu: the browser menu would open in every view.
contextMenu.label: Sync right clicks

desyncTimeoutMs.description: How long a view may take to replay a click, input or key press before it shows the desync badge, in milliseconds.
desyncTimeoutMs.help: How long a view may take to replay a click, input or key before its label shows the desync badge, in milliseconds. Raise it for slow pages, lower it to spot lagging views sooner.
desyncTimeoutMs.label: Desync timeout

detectBrowsersync.description: When a page runs Browsersync, whose ghost mode syncs clicks, scrolling and forms by itself, rBrowser switches its own sync off and says why. Switching sync on again keeps it on for that site.
detectBrowsersync.help: When a page runs Browsersync's ghost mode, which syncs clicks and scrolling itself, rBrowser switches its own sync off for that site and says so, so nothing happens twice. Off keeps rBrowser's sync on.
detectBrowsersync.label: Pause sync for Browsersync

focus.description: The field focused in the active view gets the focus in the other views too, without scrolling them. Off by default.
focus.help: The field focused in the active view gets the focus in the other views too, without scrolling them, so focus styles show everywhere. Off keeps the focus in one view.
focus.label: Sync focus

forms.description: A choice in a select, radio button, checkbox, slider, colour or date field reaches the other views as the same state, so the page's handlers see the change there too. File inputs are never synced; password values are synced but never logged.
forms.help: A choice in a select, checkbox, radio, slider, colour or date field reaches the other views as the same state and fires their change handlers. File inputs are never synced. Off, only typed text is synced.
forms.label: Sync form controls

hover.description: Hovering is replayed in the other views.
hover.help: Hovering an element in the active view hovers the same element in the other views, so hover menus and tooltips show everywhere. Off saves work on slow machines.
hover.label: Sync hover

hoverThrottleMs.description: The least time between two hover events the active view reports, in milliseconds. Higher values send fewer hover moves to the other views.
hoverThrottleMs.help: The least time between two hover positions the active view sends, in milliseconds. Raise it to 200 or more when many views make hovering stutter; lower it for smoother hover effects.
hoverThrottleMs.label: Hover throttle

input.description: Typed text is replayed in the other views.
input.help: Text typed into a field of the active view appears in the same field of the other views, so a form is filled once for every breakpoint. Off, typing stays in one view.
input.label: Sync text input

keyboard.description: Key presses are replayed in the other views.
keyboard.help: Key presses in the active view (Enter, Escape, arrows, shortcuts of the page) are replayed in the other views. Off, only the active view gets them.
keyboard.label: Sync keyboard

leaderOnlySubmit.description: Form submits and non-GET navigations run only in the active view, so a form is never sent several times.
leaderOnlySubmit.help: A form submit or a POST navigation runs only in the active view and the others follow its result, so an order or a registration is never sent several times. Off submits in every view.
leaderOnlySubmit.label: Submit only in the active view

leaderPerSession.description: With leader-only submits, every session has a leader of its own: a synced form submit is posted once per session, so each session runs its own login.
leaderPerSession.help: With leader-only submits, each session has its own leader, so a synced login is posted once per session and every session ends up signed in. Off, one view submits for all sessions.
leaderPerSession.label: One leader per session

navigation.description: Navigating in one view navigates the others.
navigation.help: Following a link or entering an address in one view takes every other view there too, so all breakpoints show the same page. Off, each view navigates on its own.
navigation.label: Sync navigation

navigationIncludeHash.description: A different fragment (#section) counts as a different page, so the other views follow hash changes too.
navigationIncludeHash.help: Whether a change of the fragment (#section) counts as a navigation the other views follow. On for pages that route by hash; off for anchors and tabs that only move within a page.
navigationIncludeHash.label: Follow hash changes

navigationSettleMs.description: How long a synced click has to take the other views to the active view's page before they load its address, in milliseconds.
navigationSettleMs.help: After a synced click the other views get this long, in milliseconds, to reach the active view's page by themselves before they load its address directly. Raise it for slow single-page apps.
navigationSettleMs.label: Navigation settle time

scroll.description: Scrolling in one view scrolls the others.
scroll.help: Scrolling one view scrolls the others to the same content, so you compare the same section at every width. Off, each view scrolls on its own.
scroll.label: Sync scrolling

scrollDebounceMs.description: How long scrolling must rest, in milliseconds, before the end position is sent to the other views once more. 0 sends it only while scrolling.
scrollDebounceMs.help: How long scrolling must rest, in milliseconds, before the final position is sent once more so every view ends at the same place. 0 sends positions only while scrolling.
scrollDebounceMs.label: Scroll end delay

scrollMode.description: Anchor brings the same content to the top of every view, whatever its width. Wheel replays the mouse wheel instead, for pages that take over scrolling themselves.
scrollMode.help: Anchor keeps the same content at the top of every view whatever its width, which suits most sites. Wheel replays the mouse wheel instead, for pages that take over scrolling with their own script.
scrollMode.label: Scroll sync mode

ffmpegPath.description: The absolute path of an ffmpeg of your own. Empty uses the LGPL build rBrowser downloads on the first recording, after you ran Video: download ffmpeg. Only your user settings can set it, never a project.
ffmpegPath.help: An ffmpeg of your own for video recordings, as an absolute path. Example: C:\Tools\ffmpeg\bin\ffmpeg.exe. Empty uses the LGPL build rBrowser downloads after Video: download ffmpeg. Only your user settings can set it.
ffmpegPath.label: Own ffmpeg

mode.description: bar shows the running activities with their controls in the activity bar; indicator draws no bar and leaves each activity to its indicator in the toolbar.
mode.help: bar (the default) shows a strip with an entry per running activity and its controls, and the toolbar shows an activity's compact indicator only while its entry is closed or switched off. indicator never draws the strip: every running activity shows as its compact indicator in the toolbar, and the views never move.
mode.label: Activity bar

position.description: Where the activity bar stands while something runs: top, below the toolbar, or bottom, above the status bar.
position.help: The activity bar appears only while something runs - a video, a recording, a flow or check run, the portal, views out of sync - with the controls of each. top puts it below the toolbar, bottom above the status bar (shown for it even while the status bar is hidden). The views give it its 28 px and take them back when the last activity ends.
position.label: Activity bar position

checks.description: A running check run, Lighthouse included, has an entry in the activity bar: the jobs through and Cancel. Off, it shows only as its indicator in the toolbar.
checks.help: Gives a running check run - Lighthouse included - an entry in the activity bar with the jobs through so far and Cancel. Off, the run shows only as its compact indicator in the toolbar.
checks.label: Check runs in the activity bar

desync.description: Views that could not follow the active view have an entry in the activity bar: how many, and Resync. Off, the desync indicator in the toolbar alone shows them.
desync.help: Gives views that could not follow the active view an entry in the activity bar with their number and Resync, which loads the active view's page in them. Off, the desync indicator in the toolbar alone shows them.
desync.label: Views out of sync in the activity bar

flows.description: A running flow, a played-back recording included, has an entry in the activity bar: the views through, Results and Cancel. Off, it shows only as its indicator in the toolbar.
flows.help: Gives a running flow - a recording played back included - an entry in the activity bar with the views through so far, Results and Cancel. Off, the run shows only as its compact indicator in the toolbar.
flows.label: Flow runs in the activity bar

portal.description: The running portal has an entry in the activity bar: its devices, a new QR code and Disconnect. Off, the portal button in the toolbar alone shows it.
portal.help: Gives the running portal an entry in the activity bar with the number of paired devices (a click opens the Portal panel), a new pairing QR code and Disconnect, which stops the portal. Off, the portal button in the toolbar alone shows it.
portal.label: Portal in the activity bar

recorder.description: A running recording has an entry in the activity bar: its steps, Pause or Resume, Add check and Stop; once stopped, Play last. Off, it shows only as its indicator in the toolbar.
recorder.help: Gives a running recording of steps an entry in the activity bar: its steps, Pause or Resume, Add check (the next click picks the element) and Stop. After it stops, the entry offers Play last until you play it, close it or start another recording. Off, the recording shows only as its indicator in the toolbar.
recorder.label: Recorder in the activity bar

video.description: A running video recording has an entry in the activity bar: its time, the views recorded and Stop. Off, it shows only as its indicator in the toolbar.
video.help: Gives a running video recording an entry in the activity bar with its time, the views it records and a Stop button. Off, the recording shows only as its compact indicator in the toolbar - its time and a stop button.
video.label: Video recording in the activity bar

address.description: When a view's label strip shows its address: differs while it is not the active view's address, always for every view, off never. The toolbar's address bar shows the active view's.
address.help: differs shows the address in the label strip of every view that is not on the active view's page - a view with its own navigation, a view that could not follow, every view while sync is off - so you see at once which page each view shows. always shows it in every strip, off in none. The tooltip has the whole address.
address.label: Address in the label strip

engineStatus.description: The engine badge of a Firefox or WebKit view says how its engine's window stands - starting, in its cell, engine stopped, window closed - with the reason in the tooltip. The badge's menu restarts a stopped engine, opens a closed window again or brings a window of its own to the front.
engineStatus.help: Shows the state of a Firefox or WebKit view's window in its engine badge, for example "Firefox · engine stopped". The badge's menu restarts the engine, opens a closed window again or brings the window to the front. Off hides the state; the engine badge and the shortcuts stay.
engineStatus.label: Engine window state in the engine badge

engineBadge.description: Every view's label strip ends in a badge naming its engine (Chromium, Firefox, WebKit); a click on it chooses another engine for the view's breakpoint. The canvas board draws the same badge.
engineBadge.help: Shows a badge with the engine at the right end of every view's label strip; click it to switch the view to Chromium, Firefox or WebKit. Off hides the badge; the shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Space, B, E) still opens the choice.
engineBadge.label: Engine badge

fileNameTime.description: The time in the names of new screenshot and video folders, recordings and sitemap and compare runs: your local time or UTC.
fileNameTime.help: local names them in the time of your system, daylight saving time included; utc in Coordinated Universal Time. Folders and recordings already made keep their names, and the lists sort them by when they were made. The times stored inside the files are always UTC.
fileNameTime.label: Time in file names

firstRunWizard.description: The setup wizard opens by itself at the very first start, and a project folder without a config says "Set up project" once in the status bar.
firstRunWizard.help: Off: neither happens, and the command that opens the wizard (Ctrl+Shift+Space, Comma, W) does nothing - for a team that rolls out its own setup. rBrowser works fully without the wizard.
firstRunWizard.label: Setup wizard

followWindowsTextSize.description: rBrowser's own windows grow with the Windows text size (Accessibility > Text size, 100 to 225 %) and follow a change at once. Off keeps them at 100 %. The pages in the views are not affected.
followWindowsTextSize.help: Follows the Windows setting Settings > Accessibility > Text size: the toolbar, the status bar, the label strips and breakpoint bars, the settings, the palette and the panel dock grow with it, and the views move to make room. A change in Windows applies at once, without a restart. Off keeps rBrowser at 100 %. The pages in the views keep their size; zoom them with the page zoom.
followWindowsTextSize.label: Follow the Windows text size

highlightActiveView.description: The label strip of the active view, the one the others follow, is drawn in the accent colour in the grid, focus, horizontal and split layouts. The canvas marks its active label itself.
highlightActiveView.help: Draws the label strip of the active view, the one the others follow, in the accent colour, so you always see which view leads. Off shows every label the same.
highlightActiveView.label: Mark the active view

language.help: The language of rBrowser's own interface: menus, settings, messages. English only until more languages arrive; the pages in the views keep their own language.
language.label: Language

devices.description: The New size list (Ctrl+Shift+Space, V, *; New size… in the add menus) offers the device presets below the sizes: the built-in ones and your own, each with its size and pixel ratio. Off leaves the sizes and Custom….
devices.help: Lists the device presets in the New size list, below the sizes. Choosing a device opens a view with its size, pixel ratio, user agent and touch. Off keeps the list short: the sizes and Custom…, where you type a size of your own.
devices.label: Devices in the New size list

openLinksIn.description: Where a link from rBrowser opens - a finding's help page, a plugin panel's report or help link: your browser, the active view, or ask each time.
openLinksIn.help: system opens the link in the default browser of Windows, activeView loads it in the grid's active view (with navigation sync on, in every view), ask offers both on every link. Only http and https links open; anything else is refused.
openLinksIn.label: Open links in

pageContextMenu.description: The page's context menu offers rBrowser's entries below Chromium's: Inspect element, DevTools, Screenshot, Video, Checks and Panels for the clicked view. Off leaves Chromium's menu and "Do not sync the next click"; the commands and their shortcuts stay.
pageContextMenu.help: Adds rBrowser's entries to the right-click menu of every page: inspect the element under the cursor, open DevTools, screenshots and video of this or all views, the checks and the panels - all for the view you clicked. Off keeps Chromium's own menu plus "Do not sync the next click"; every entry stays reachable through its shortcut and the command palette.
pageContextMenu.label: rBrowser entries in the page's context menu

pageContextMenuEmulation.description: Offer the toolbar's emulation switches for the clicked view in the page's context menu - colour scheme, reduced motion, offline, location, time zone, reset - and Analyze breakpoints beside them.
pageContextMenuEmulation.help: Whether a page's context menu has the Emulation submenu: the colour scheme (light, dark or no override), reduced motion, offline, location and time zone presets and Reset for the clicked view, the same for all views, each with its current state marked, and Analyze breakpoints as an entry of the menu. Off, the submenu is gone and Analyze breakpoints stays under Checks. It belongs to "Page context menu" (ui.pageContextMenu): with that switch off the whole block is gone and this one has no effect.
pageContextMenuEmulation.label: Emulation in the page's context menu

canvasZoom.description: While the canvas layout is shown, the right of the status bar shows the canvas zoom: the active view's page zoom, a slider, minus and plus buttons and the presets.
canvasZoom.help: Shows the canvas zoom at the right of the status bar while the canvas layout is shown. The number is the active view's page zoom: 100 % shows its page at its real size. Drag the slider, press minus or plus, or pick a preset (Fit, 25 to 200 %). Ctrl+0 on the canvas board sets 100 %; Ctrl+Shift+Space, L, 0 does the same anywhere.
canvasZoom.label: Canvas zoom in the status bar

historySize.description: How many messages the history keeps (10 to 1000); the oldest go first.
historySize.help: How many messages the status bar's history keeps (10 to 1000); the oldest drop out first. Raise it when you review a long run afterwards.
historySize.label: Messages kept

infoTimeoutSec.description: Seconds an info or success message stays in the status bar (0 to 600); 0 keeps it until the next message. Warnings and errors stay until you close them.
infoTimeoutSec.help: How long an info or success message stays in the status bar, in seconds (0 to 600); 0 keeps it until the next message. Warnings and errors stay until you close them.
infoTimeoutSec.label: Info stays for

visible.description: The bar at the bottom of the window with the latest message and the message history. Hidden, the views take its room and messages still reach the history (Ctrl+Shift+Space P L).
visible.help: Shows the bar at the bottom with the latest message and the history. Hidden, the views take its room; messages still reach the history (Ctrl+Shift+Space, P, L).
visible.label: Show the status bar

syntaxHighlight.description: Code shows in syntax colours: values, stack traces, request and response bodies and headers, snippets and storage values in the plugin panels, and the JSON view of the settings window.
syntaxHighlight.help: Colours code wherever rBrowser shows it - the console's values and stack traces, the network panel's bodies and headers, snippets, storage values and the settings' JSON view - in both themes. Off shows code in one colour. More than 200 KiB is always one colour.
syntaxHighlight.label: Syntax colours

theme.description: Light, dark, or follow the system.
theme.help: Light or dark for rBrowser's own windows, or system to follow Windows. The pages in the views are not affected; use Emulation > Colour scheme for them.
theme.label: Theme

overflow.description: What the toolbar does with what does not fit into a narrow window: menu moves it into the main menu ≡ at the right end, wrap breaks the toolbar into a second row and the views move down. The address bar and back, forward and reload always stay.
overflow.help: What happens to the toolbar's controls when the window is too narrow for them. menu: the wide lists shrink to icons first, then the controls move into the main menu ≡ at the right end, the least used first. wrap: they go into a second row and the views start lower; what a second row does not hold either goes into the menu. The address bar keeps at least 240 px either way.
overflow.label: Toolbar in a narrow window

panelsToggle.description: A switch at the right end of the toolbar that opens the plugin panels and folds them to their icon rail again, lit while they are open. Off by default: the icon rail beside the views opens them, as do the commands and the shortcut.
panelsToggle.help: Shows a button at the right end of the toolbar that opens the plugin panels - docked at their size, or their own window - and folds them back to the icon rail, highlighted while they are open; a dot marks it while a panel a command opened waits in the rail. Its tooltip names the shortcut (Ctrl+Shift+Space, P, Z). In a narrow window it is the last control to move into the "More" menu. Off by default, since the icon rail beside the views does the same; a value you set yourself stays.
panelsToggle.label: Plugin panels switch in the toolbar

portalButton.description: A button in the toolbar that starts the portal and pairs a phone or tablet in the LAN, with the number of paired devices on it. Off, the button is gone; the Portal panel, the command palette and the shortcuts still run the portal.
portalButton.help: Shows a phone-and-tablet button in the toolbar for the portal, which mirrors the active view to real devices in your network. Its name and tooltip say the state: off, on without a device, or on with the number of paired devices, which also stands on the button. While the portal is off, a click starts it and shows a QR code to pair a device - only when the portal is allowed under Portal and pairing in Security & Privacy. While it runs, a click opens a menu: show a new QR code, the devices, disconnect one device or all of them, stop the portal. In a narrow window it moves into the "More" menu. Off removes the button only: the portal still starts with Ctrl+Shift+Space, S, P, from the command palette and in the Portal panel.
portalButton.label: Portal button in the toolbar

viewContextMenu.description: The menus of the views: on a view's label strip (a click on the active view's, a right-click on any view's, in every layout) Remove view, Set as active, Size, Engine and Pop out; on the free canvas, an empty cell or the toolbar's + the hidden breakpoints to add. Off leaves the strips and the canvas as before; the + button, the shortcuts, the palette and MCP stay.
viewContextMenu.help: Shows the view menus: on a view's label strip (click the active view's label, or right-click any view's label) Remove view, Set as active, Size, Engine and Pop out; on the free canvas or an empty cell the breakpoints to add. Off leaves the strips and the canvas without them; the + button, the shortcuts, the palette and MCP still add and remove views.
viewContextMenu.label: View menus

align.description: Where the breakpoint bar's text stands: center puts it in the middle of the strip, every line; start at the strip's left edge.
align.help: center (the default) puts the breakpoint bar's text in the middle of the strip under each view, in each of its lines. start puts it at the left edge, as before.
align.label: Breakpoint bar text alignment

analyze.description: Reads the media queries of the page a view shows from the loaded page itself, after every load, so the breakpoint bar names the page's own min-width and max-width queries. Nothing is requested a second time. Off, the breakpoint bar names the ends of the breakpoint's range, or what Analyze Breakpoints found.
analyze.help: On, the breakpoint bar names the step of the page each view shows, from its media queries, for example 1024-1279px | md. rBrowser reads them from the page that is already loaded, shortly after every load; it requests nothing again and writes nothing to the project. A stylesheet from another origin that the page itself may not read is left out; the breakpoint bar's tooltip says how many. Off, or until a page is read, the breakpoint bar names the breakpoint's range, for example 768-1023px, or what Analyze Breakpoints found. If the page's stylesheets cannot all be read, what Analyze Breakpoints found is kept.
analyze.label: Read the page's media queries for the breakpoint bar

fields.description: What the breakpoint bar names, always in this order: breakpoint (its id), range (from which width to which the page's step holds; the breakpoint's range until the page was read), size (width, height and pixel ratio of the view), queries (the step's ends as min-width and max-width) and framework (the page's class for the width, when the analysis recognised one). Range and framework by default.
fields.help: Choose what the breakpoint bar under a view names. By default range and class, for example 1024-1279px | md. Once the page was read (by itself after every load with "Read the page's media queries for the breakpoint bar", or by Analyze Breakpoints: Ctrl+Shift+Space, B, A) the range is the page's own step: on a mobile-first page from its min-width to the next min-width minus 1. Until then it is the breakpoint's range. queries names the same step as min-width and max-width, never the same side twice; the tooltip names every query of the page that holds. A view whose chosen fields all have no value shows no breakpoint bar and keeps its height; with no field left none is shown.
fields.label: Breakpoint bar fields

lighthouse.description: A bar under every view, below the vitals bar, in every layout and in a view's own window: the four Lighthouse scores - Performance, Accessibility, Best Practices and SEO - of the newest Lighthouse run of the page the view shows at its breakpoint, each in Lighthouse's colour with the shape of its rating (circle 90-100, square 50-89, triangle 0-49). A view without such a run has no bar. The view gives it 18 px of its height.
lighthouse.help: Shows the Lighthouse bar under every view, for example "● 96 Performance  ■ 72 Accessibility  ● 100 SEO": the shape and colour tell the rating, a narrow view names the categories short (Perf, A11y, BP, SEO) or not at all. Only a run of the page the view shows now, at its breakpoint, counts - another page has no bar until it was measured. The tooltip names when the run was made (local time) and every score in words; a click opens the run's report. In a low view the breakpoint bar's first line stays longest, then the vitals bar, then the Lighthouse bar. Off gives the views the height back; MCP's lighthouse_reports still reads the scores. Ctrl+Shift+Space, O, G switches it, and the page's context menu has it beside the other bars.
lighthouse.label: Lighthouse bar under every view

visible.description: A strip in the breakpoint's colour under every view, in every layout and in a view's own window: by default the widths the page's step holds for and the page's class for them. The view gives it 18 px of its height, never more than half of it.
visible.help: Shows the breakpoint bar (formerly called the footer), a coloured strip under every view. By default it names the widths the page's step holds for and the page's class for them, for example 1024-1279px | md; the breakpoint's name and the view's size stand in the label strip above, and "Breakpoint bar fields" adds them. Give a breakpoint its own colour in Settings > Breakpoints ("color" in the project config); it applies when saved, and the text turns black or white to stay readable. A breakpoint bar never takes more than half of its view: in a low view, such as a canvas zoomed far out, it keeps one line or steps aside. Off gives the views the height back; Ctrl+Shift+Space, O, B switches it.
visible.label: Breakpoint bar under every view

vitals.description: A bar under every view, below the breakpoint bar, in every layout and in a view's own window: the view's Core Web Vitals - LCP, CLS and INP - each with the shape of its rating (circle good, square needs improvement, triangle poor), and a warning when the view uses much CPU or memory. The view gives it 18 px of its height.
vitals.help: Shows the vitals bar under every view, for example "● LCP 1.84 s  ▲ CLS 0.30  INP –": the shape tells the rating, a dash a vital not measured yet. The tooltip has all five vitals with their ratings in words; a click marks the element behind the worst rated vital in the view. Needs Web Vitals (or the resource readings) switched on. In a low view the breakpoint bar's first line stays longest, then the vitals bar. Off gives the views the height back; MCP's view_metrics still reads the vitals. Ctrl+Shift+Space, O, W switches it, and the page's context menu has it beside the breakpoint bar.
vitals.label: Vitals bar under every view

wrap.description: What the breakpoint bar does in a view too narrow for its text: auto breaks it into a second line between two fields, and the view gives the breakpoint bar the height of two lines; never keeps one line that ends in an ellipsis. What still does not fit is in the tooltip.
wrap.help: In a narrow view, for example a 375 px phone breakpoint in a full grid, the breakpoint bar's text is wider than the view. auto (the default) breaks it between two fields into a second line, and the view gives the breakpoint bar 36 px instead of 18; the breakpoint bars of the views beside it stay at the same bottom edge. never keeps one line and cuts its end. Whatever even two lines cannot show is cut at the end; hover the breakpoint bar to read all of it in the tooltip.
wrap.label: Breakpoint bar in a narrow view

autoInstall.description: When a downloaded update installs by itself: off (only when you ask) or when rBrowser quits.
autoInstall.help: When a downloaded update installs by itself: off installs only when you ask, on-quit installs when rBrowser closes.
autoInstall.label: Install updates automatically

cefAgeWarning.description: Show a notice when the built-in Chromium (CEF) is older than six weeks and updates are not checked by themselves.
cefAgeWarning.help: Shows a notice when the built-in Chromium (CEF) is older than six weeks and updates are not checked at the start, so you know the engine is behind. Off never warns.
cefAgeWarning.label: Warn about an old browser engine

channel.description: Automatic, stable releases only, or pre-releases too.
channel.help: Which releases self-update offers. Automatic (the default) follows the build: a pre-release build reads the pre-releases, a release build the stable releases. Stable or Beta chooses for good.
channel.label: Update channel

check.description: When rBrowser looks for a newer version: off, or once at every start.
check.help: When rBrowser looks for a newer version: off, or once at every start. A found update is shown with its Install and restart button; it installs only when you click it or, with Install updates automatically on quit, when rBrowser closes.
check.label: Check for updates

enabled.description: Let rBrowser update itself from signed releases. Off: nothing is fetched and nothing installed.
enabled.help: Lets rBrowser update itself from signed releases. Off, nothing is fetched or installed; update by unpacking the new ZIP.
enabled.label: Self-update

keepOnReload.description: A zoomed page keeps its zoom when it reloads or navigates, as Chromium keeps it per site. Off, every load starts at 100%.
keepOnReload.help: Keeps a view's page zoom across reloads and navigation, as Chromium does. Off, every page a view loads starts at 100%, so the breakpoint's width always applies as set.
keepOnReload.label: Keep the page zoom on reload

keys.description: With the focus in a page, Ctrl+0 sets the view's page zoom back to 100% and Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus zoom it in Chromium's steps, as in Chrome. Off, the keys reach the page.
keys.help: Ctrl+0, Ctrl+Plus and Ctrl+Minus zoom the page of the view that has the focus, as in Chrome. Off, the keys reach the page; the commands, the zoom badge in the label strip and MCP stay. On the canvas board Ctrl+0 stays the canvas zoom.
keys.label: Zoom keys in a page

sync.description: A page zoom applies to every view at once. Off, it is the view's own - except that Chromium keeps the zoom per site, so views of one session showing the same host zoom together.
sync.help: Applies a page zoom - from the keys, the wheel, a command or MCP - to every view at once. Off, the zoom is the view's own; Chromium still keeps it per site, so views of one session on the same host zoom together, and each one's badge says so.
sync.label: Zoom every view together

wheel.description: Ctrl and the mouse wheel over a page zoom it, as in Chromium. Off, rBrowser puts a zoom the wheel made back at once.
wheel.help: Ctrl and the mouse wheel zoom the page under the pointer, as in Chromium. Off, rBrowser sets a zoom the wheel made back at once; the keys, the commands and MCP still zoom.
wheel.label: Zoom with Ctrl and the wheel

failOnMetaMismatch.description: Report a comparison against a baseline taken with another monitor DPI, engine version, viewport or full-page setting as an error instead of a warning.
failOnMetaMismatch.help: Treat a comparison against a baseline taken with another monitor DPI, engine version, viewport or full-page setting as an error instead of a warning, so a changed setup cannot pass unnoticed.
failOnMetaMismatch.label: Fail on a different setup

fullPage.description: Compare and save the whole page, not only the visible viewport.
fullPage.help: Whether a baseline and a comparison cover the whole scrolled page or only the visible viewport. Full page catches changes below the fold; the viewport is faster.
fullPage.label: Full page

lfsCheck.description: After saving a baseline, check that Git LFS stores .rbrowser/baselines and is installed, and offer the set-up when not.
lfsCheck.help: After saving a baseline, check that Git LFS is installed and tracks .rbrowser/baselines, and offer the set-up when not, so image files do not bloat the repository. Off skips the check.
lfsCheck.label: Check Git LFS

slugStrategy.description: How a page's address names its baseline folder: the path only (local and staging share baselines), the host and the path, or the path and the query.
slugStrategy.help: How a page's address names its baseline folder: path only lets local and staging share baselines, host and path keeps them apart, path and query tells ?page=2 from ?page=3.
slugStrategy.label: Baseline folder name

threshold.description: How different two pixels may be and still count as equal, from 0 (exactly equal) to 1 (anything goes). Anti-aliased edges are tolerated apart from it.
threshold.help: How different two pixels may be and still count as equal in a visual comparison, from 0 (exact) to 1 (anything). 0.1 ignores rendering noise; lower it to catch subtle colour changes.
threshold.label: Colour tolerance

enabled.description: Measure LCP, CLS, INP, FCP and TTFB in every view and show them in its vitals bar.
enabled.help: Measures LCP, CLS, INP, FCP and TTFB in every view and shows them in the vitals bar under it, so you compare page speed across breakpoints. Off measures nothing.
enabled.label: Show Web Vitals

thresholds.description: The good and poor limit per metric (ms; CLS without unit). Up to good is good, above poor is poor. Default: the thresholds of web.dev.
thresholds.help: The limits that colour each metric's badge: up to good is green, above poor is red, between is orange. Milliseconds, CLS without a unit. Example: lcp good 2500, poor 4000, the web.dev thresholds.
thresholds.label: Rating thresholds

distro.description: The WSL distribution the helper runs in. Empty uses the project's distribution, else the WSL default.
distro.help: The WSL distribution the file watcher and the CDP tunnel run in. Example: Ubuntu-24.04. Empty uses the distribution of the project's path, else the WSL default.
distro.label: WSL distribution

helperPath.description: Another rbrowser-wsl helper than the one rBrowser ships, as a Linux or Windows path. Empty uses the packaged one.

networkingModeOverride.description: Whether tools inside WSL reach rBrowser on 127.0.0.1. Auto detects the WSL networking mode; mirrored or NAT sets it by hand.
networkingModeOverride.help: Whether tools inside WSL reach rBrowser on 127.0.0.1: auto detects WSL's networking mode, mirrored says they do, nat says they need the tunnel.
networkingModeOverride.label: WSL networking mode
